    Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win

    📅 23 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 26 min read (5162 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~26 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning.
    • The narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image.
    • All of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

    The narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct concerns with City that Maresca must fix. A new midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

    All of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

    Sources indicate that A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guéhi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass, before City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

    According to recent reports, joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur.

    In a recent development, “It’s the perfect day to be honest,” Maresca mentioned, although he may wish to set his expectations slightly higher. The East Stand which faces the dugouts at the Etihad unfurled a banner before the game welcoming him back to Manchester after his spell as Guardiola’s assistant. “I was very pleased when the game started, to watch the banner at the other side, and I was pleased at the end because we gave them the joy of the three points.”.

    His team made a fluid and furious start to Premier League football, suffused with a desire to prove the Community Shield is just a jumped-up friendly. A newly streamlined short-haired Erling Haaland ran with impatience, Elliot Anderson was a sinewy presence in midfield, Foden pulled off a gorgeous flick which led to a shot by Rico Lewis, well saved by Djordje Petrovic.

    It has been revealed that maresca’s selection was surprising, with six defenders in his XI, some deployed unexpectedly. Guéhi partnered Anderson in defensive midfield, while their England team-mate O’Reilly was often just behind Haaland in a No 10 role. There was an air of destiny about one O’Reilly run down the left flank in the first half, cruising to the byline and crossing presentably. Haaland was well positioned in the middle, but utterly fluffed his lines. Samson similes on standby, although perhaps he too was short of full match fitness during his early-season visit from the Philistines?

    Momentum shifted after Haaland’s miss, and Bournemouth took the lead when an innocuous high ball flummoxed Abdukodir Khusanov and Rúben Dias. They both pursued it, neither could make decisive contact and it left Evanilson on the ball with space to manufacture an unmissable cross for Marcus Tavernier.

    Recent findings suggest that marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc.

    In a recent development, marco Rose, their new manager, is facing a similarly daunting task to Maresca in living up to a predecessor who led Bournemouth to their highest-ever league finish and European football. “How the game went, it was quite unlucky to lose,” he remarked. “We had two situations, one corner kick and one attacking when we defended too passive, and that’s why we lost.”.

    His team showed an appealing coiled-spring quality after weathering the early City onslaught. They have players of class with the ever lively Tavernier, new signing António Silva seamlessly replacing Marcos Senesi at centre-back and silky Alex Scott, the Guernsey Grealish, whose current standing has now overtaken the man who gave him his nickname.

    They could not hang on here though, with Guéhi atoning for a free header planted wide with his day-saving equaliser. Cherki’s corner was nodded in from around the six-yard line then, with the game in the balance, the Frenchman provided another, thanks in part to the semi-automated gods smiling on Gvardiol and his newly introduced manager.

    "That is an EXTRAORDINARY miss!" 🫣Marc Guehi misses a golden opportunity to equalise for Manchester City! pic.twitter.com/Jl96MMmQeP.

    No mistakes this time from Marc Guehi 😤 pic.twitter.com/xlCJXWUzz6.

    City will need more, especially in midfield. Anderson at his best can cover the ground and roles of two men, which is just as well as City await reinforcements. The incoming Ayyoub Bouaddi will help, but it is a big ask for an 18-year-old to fill a spot vacated by a Ballon d’Or winner. Maresca was asked after the match about finding a “newly introduced Rodri” and deadpanned “Marc Guéhi”, who played acceptably, but is probably not a long-term solution.

    Industry observers note that there was a jadedness at times from City, which is not a great way to start the season, although they will surely improve with a bolstered squad and fitness levels. Maresca noted “four or five” of his players who returned late from the World Cup are still effectively in pre-season training, including Haaland and Anderson.

    Of course City are not the finished article, what team are one game into a upcoming season? While there is a vast gap from this performance to their best, it was still impressive to smuggle three points from zero with six minutes left to play. Guardiola’s influence will be hard to shake, but that need not be a negative.

    Marc Guéhi: Central Midfield Edition pic.twitter.com/ViBZqOroB2.

    Sources indicate that the Maresca era begins with the most dramatic of wins. City were trailing 1-0 at 84 minutes, but somehow managed to turn it around.

    Emery doesn’t hang around. I’m not convinced he shook Hurzeler’s hand.

    Manchester City 2 Bournemouth 1 (Gvardiol) Oh my, Gvardiol has the ball in the back of the net but his “winner” is ruled out by the linesman instantly. Cherki had wriggled this way and that on the edge of the box before sliding in the Croatian who dispatched the ball with aplomb.

    BUT, replays show that Hill’s back foot played Gvardiol onside ...so the late, late goal is GIVEN!

    According to recent reports, maresca jumps for joy, the Etihad erupts. But that is heartbreaking for Bournemouth...

    Recent findings suggest that joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur.

    Guehi saves the day for City, scoring a harder header than the sitter he missed early in this half. Nice corner from Cherki was powererd in from close to the penalty spot. Crowd smells blood with five minutes left but Bournemouth look to still have a bit in the tank.

    Incidentally, Jack Grealish is on for City with the ‘Guernsey Grealish’ Alex Scott still out there for Bournemouth, who is presumably worth about double in today’s transfer market? Can’t be often that a player shares pitch with his nickname-giver as their careers head in opposite direction. Wonder if Lionel Messi was ever described as “the new Roman Riquelme?” and played against him?

    According to recent reports, bournemouth have responded well to getting pegged back, playing through City, who are desperate for a shot at three points. Gannon-Doak stands up a cross but finds the gloves of Donnarumma.

    City attempt to break down the left but Grealish just runs out of road.

    Manchester City 1 Bournemouth 1 (Guehi) He might have missed a sitter earlier on, but when presented with a similar opportunity from a corner - this time via Cherki from the right - Guehi makes no mistake, planting his header beyond Petrovic.

    No mistakes this time from Marc Guehi 😤 pic.twitter.com/xlCJXWUzz6.

    Haaland threatens to break free down Bournemouth’s right but Truffert just about recovers and clears his lines.

    Grealish replaces Foden, who slopes straight down the tunnel.

    Jebbison calls Donnarumma - who has been a spectator for the past 20 minutes - into action with a sharp header. There is a delay in the taking of the subsequent corner as Adams and Jebbison jostle for position with the City goalkeeper, but it’s all for nothing as the delivery is dealt with.

    Industry observers note that foden goes into the book for a foul on substitute Jebbison. A tad harsh, perhaps. Looks like he semi-slipped into that contact.

    According to recent reports, ayari attempts an bicycle kick but cannot beat Bizot. That would have been a goal of the month contender had it found the back of the net.

    Guehi combines with Foden down the right and hits the by-line before a digging out a cross to Haaland. The ball is behind him and his right-footed effort does not have the requisite power to beat Petrovic, who has been immense today.

    Bit better from City, Foden curls just wide, Semenyo has a shot well saved by Petrovic. Meres presence of Cherki seems to have injected some urgency to their attacks and fear to Bournemouth’s defence. Not sure City look quite ready for this season. Obviously there will be further incomings but they are leggier and more haphazard than Bournemouth.

    Chance! Foden, Nunes and Cherki work the ball from right to left on the edge of Bournemouth’s box, eventually falling to Haaland who scoops the ball over with his usually lethal left boot. The visitors had plenty of men between ball and goal and that caused the Norwegian to snatch at his effort.

    Villa started last season with no win in their first five games and just three points. They then rallied strongly after that. This one feels different as the rebuild is so significant. Second half has been very flat so far.

    City are asking questions now. Cherki combines with Foden down the right and the Englishman shifts the ball on to his favoured left boot and his curled effort deflects off Silva and out for a corner which comes to nothing.

    Semenyo breaks free down the left channel and fires the ball across the keeper towards the far post, but Petrovic gets a strong hand to it and pulls off a good save.

    Kostoulas thinks he’s made it five having followed in a fizzed-in Costinha effort that had struck the post. But the strike is scrubbed off immediately and replays back up the linesman’s decision.

    According to recent reports, little sign of City finding the composure to take control of this match. Passing is getting ever-sloppier and Guehi put a free header painfully wide. Maresca’s team are dominating possession but would be no surprise if the next goal was another Bournemouth sucker-punch. Kovacic and Cherki about to come on, the latter should improve the picture.

    Anderson receives treatment on the pitch and is subsequently replaced by Kovacic. The Englishman stretches out his right leg as he leaves the field of play and keeps it elevated as he takes his position on the bench.

    Sources indicate that dunk creates some chaos in Villa’s box, spinning in a lofted through-ball which Bizot palms away under duress. Rutter then pulls an effort wide off the resulting corner.

    According to recent reports, nunes makes an instant impact, beating Scott easily down the right before standing up a cross to the far post where Haaland is waiting. Two Bournemouth defenders mirror the forward’s leap and do enough to disrupt his flow - and Semenyo’s - the Ghanaian also misses the ball.

    In a recent development, shows how few options Emery has - he has not made a change at half-time. Villa have been a little brighter going forward. A good run from Hemmings to play in Maatsen, and then the Villa teenager misjudging a cross when McGinn put him in down the right. But Brighton will feel there are more goals for them.

    Maresca looks to his bench and brings on Nunes for Lewis.

    Industry observers note that brighton are still going for this. Gross’ corner from the left reaches Vuskovic at the back post, but he cannot poke the ball past Bizot.

    According to recent reports, you’ll do well to see a worse miss all season! Guehi is afforded the freedom of Manchester inside the box from an inswinging corner but he somehow glances the ball wide.

    "That is an EXTRAORDINARY miss!" 🫣Marc Guehi misses a golden opportunity to equalise for Manchester City! pic.twitter.com/Jl96MMmQeP.

    According to recent reports, de Cuyper tees up another corner from the right. His punched-in delivery picks out Ayari perfectly on the edge of the box but the Swede’s volley flies just wide. A touch ball to hit first time.

    Villa have opted to sit in and hope they can see this out without further damage. The Sky Sports cameras pan to a now sparse away end where some are still cheering their side on. Fair play.

    Play has resumed at the Etihad and immediately City begin circulating the ball in front of Bournemouth’s first line of pressure. It’s all very slow still and they are unable to penetrate their opponents’ robust mid-black.

    We’re back under way at the Amex.

    According to recent reports, boos at half time as City leave the field, although will charitably assume they are more for referee Jared Gillet for his late non-award of a penalty. Rico Lewis went down in the box but it looked soft. Another early test for Maresca, Bournemouth are lively in attack and defending capably. City all pace and intent but not playing with much patience or finesse.

    Pretty horrifying first half from Villa. It was a strange team to start with – factoring in the four significant summer sales and then the two absentees, Watkins and Emi Martinez. But this has been even worse than expected. Many of the team has just crumbled under the first sign of pressure. Pau Torres has been terrible. Joao Gomes picked up a yellow and then a red card on his debut. Villa started with Buendia as a centre-forward and now - with ten men - are just trying to play without any striker at all. Emery’s options are limited. Funny to think they started really well and should have taken the lead through Buendia on five minutes.

    Industry observers note that there’s a shout for a penalty as Haaland knocks down a header at the back post for Lewis, who gets shoved to the ground clumsily by Scott. Nothing going though, and that’s the half.

    A nightmare start for Emery’s side.

    There’s a coming together on the halfway line at the Etihad. Haaland and Silva tangle, which sets off a chain reaction as Kluivert comes steaming in, first towards Haaland and then Guehi. Evanilson is next on the scene and he gets a firm shove off Gvardiol.

    In a recent development, city now looking shaky at the back. Cross-field balls in their half zipping past half a dozen in sky blue without intervention, shots from range going just wide, Donnarumma needing to save well to prevent a second.

    Has stopped clicking up front as well, something isn’t going to plan when you have Haaland in your team but most of the high balls are heading towards Foden and O’Reilly.

    Industry observers note that CARTÃO VERMELHO! Gomes is sent off. Disaster for Villa. It was a kick at Rutter borne of frustration. McGinn was already walking Gomes away from referee Peter Bankes before the decision came. A clear kick to the chest after Rutter knocked him over. Gomes has been nowhere near the level required. He will never forget his Villa debut.

    According to recent reports, ooof, Tavernier goes close with a lovely curled effort from 25 yards out. Just wide, however.

    Kluivert gets a sight at goal moments later but is denied by Donnarumma who gets down to his left sharply to keep the ball out.

    Haaland looks to breathe life into City’s rather drab performance by chasing down Petrovic.

    Moments later, he directs a glancing header towards goal and forces the Bournemouth keeper into a smart stop. Foden’s subsequent corner is not up to much.

    VAR is looking at an incident on the halfway line. Rutter barges into Gomes and the midfielder kicks out at the Brighton front man. The referee is sent to the screen and a red card correctly follows. A dreadful performance from Gomes.

    Villa have really struggled under pressure at the back. Going forward they still look have enough creative players that they are not embarrassed. But Brighton are dominating them with the press in the Villa half. There are not many options for Emery to change at half-time. Mings? Garnacho?

    It has been revealed that some very untidy defending for the opening goal here which comes against the run of play, if not drastically so. Khusanov was bamboozled by an  innocuous high ball, couldn’t make decisive contact and left space for it to reach Evanlison on the right, whose cross was hard for Tavernier to miss.

    Recent findings suggest that A few groans and grumbles already from the home fans, Guehi getting some flak for squandering a decent position near the Bournemouth area and giving away the ball. Not really his job to be on the ball and making stuff happen near the opposition box though, is it?

    This is looking very bad for Villa. Two Brighton goals in one minute for Jack Hinshelwood and it is 4-0 with 31 mins played. The first was a very well-worked goal – Ayari cross nodded down by Gomez for Hinshelwood to head in. The second was just another mistake by Villa – Ayari stealing the ball from Joao Gomes to create a critical turnover. Villa started well but they look completely outgunned physically. Brighton are really pressing home their advantage in the duels. Lots of pressure on the likes of young George Hemmings and Gomes.

    Sources indicate that "Absolutely INCREDIBLE!"Jack Hinshelwood scores two in a matter of minutes and Brighton are ripping Aston Villa apart! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/tvS5qMJJ8C.

    Brighton 4 Aston Villa 0 (Hinshelwood) That’s two in a matter of seconds. Again, Villa try to play out from the back and again they get caught out. Ayari telescopes in a leg to take the ball away from Gomes on the edge of Villa’s box and Hinshelwood is there to tuck it home.

    Brighton 3 Aston Villa 0 (Hinshelwood) A cross from the left is nodded back across goal by Gomez and Hinshelwood is there to finish.

    Recent findings suggest that manchester City 0 Bournemouth 1 (Tavernier) Bournemouth carve City open with ease. A long ball from Smith is not dealt with and Rayan works the ball out to Evanilson who needs just a brief look up before picking out Tavernier, who finishes at the back post.

    Marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc.

    It has been revealed that city have not yet reached the intensity levels they usually show when in full swing. Semenyo tries to inject some energy with a burst down the left but Rayan does well to track back and cut it out.

    Villa’s defence is floundering. This time a corner delivered from the right sails over everyone, including Bizot, but the back-post nod-down evades everyone and Villa clear their lines.

    Bright start from City, but momentum has diminished since an odd miss from Haaland, whose limbs looked unusually muddled after O’Reilly soared down the left wing and crossed presentably. Move had an air of inevitability to it, was unexpected not to see the Norwegian score. Prepare the Samson similes.

    The second goal from Brighton, and it’s direct. Georginio Rutter played through with a very straight ball, and Rutter had Pau Torres on the proverbial toast. De Cuyper kept up with his team-mate and ran onto the cross. Villa have not been bad. Torres, however, is having a dreadful afternoon.

    Sources indicate that brighton 2 Aston Villa 0 (De Cuyper) Rutter does brilliantly to latch on to a ball over the top from well inside his half. He bursts down the left channel before lashing a fierce ball across the face of goal which De Cuyper turns in. Villa in all sorts of problems here.

    What a start for Brighton!Maxim De Cuyper doubles their advantage! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/3WbyZlEhMV.

    Chance! O’Reilly bursts past Smith out on the left and picks out Haaland, who appears to be in two minds as to whether he wants to head or volley the ball. Instead he does neither and the chance goes begging.

    Sources indicate that gomes leaves one on Ayari, which is risky given he has already picked up a booking. A red card at this point would be hugely damaging.

    Industry observers note that brighton take the lead with an own goal from Victor Lindelof. An unfortunate one for the Swede who was trying to get Maxim De Cuyper’s shot off the line. It hit the post and ricocheted in off Lindelof. The fault lay with Pau Torres who gave the ball away needlessly. Very good turn from De Cuyper to make the room for the shot. Up until then, Villa - even with this unusual understrength side - were much the better.

    Industry observers note that lewis is in fact playing right-back, with Guehi into defensive midfield alongside Anderson. O’Reilly advanced of both, with Gvardiol at left-back. All quite fluid, though, as you would expect from modern City.

    Brighton 1 Aston Villa 0 (OG Lindelof) A disaster at the back for Villa. Pau Torres looks to play out from near the by-line but instead picks out De Cuyper inside Villa’s box. The wide man does well to steady himself before getting a shot away, which ricochets off the post, back on to Lindelof and into the net.

    Industry observers note that city have started brightly. Here Haaland slips in Lewis, who is unmissable with his upcoming bleached hair, but Petrovic pulls off a smart save.

    It has been revealed that chance! Ayari gets his pocket picked inside his own half by a buzzing Barkley. Buendia has a sight of goal but he slides the ball inches wide.

    He’s at it again moments later, but he sends a third effort at goal over the bar.

    According to recent reports, villa have started the brighter of the two sides. McGinn spins a deep free-kick into the box, which is cleared out to Buendia on the edge of the box but his shot sails over.

    A warm minute’s applause for the former Manchester City manager.

    Brighton are in their customary blue and white home kits shooting left to right, with Villa in black.

    Sources indicate that that’s a “Welcome Back Enzo” banner slowly cascading down the East stand. Feel that the tifo department has missed a trick, because it would have been very amusing to use a picture of Pep Guardiola, and see if anyone noticed. That could actually be Guardiola for all I know, my facial recognition is dreadful. Getting all of the trite “don’t they look similar!” observations out of my system ahead of the September cut-off point.

    The teams have emerged from the tunnel at the Amex and the Etihad...

    When asked by Sky Sports whether Ollie Watkins’ omission from the match-day squad was a sign that his Villa career was over, Emery pursed his lips and stared back at the reporter for a few seconds before saying: “Silence.”.

    After being pressed on the subject, he added: “No, no, no. We are playing today here. It’s OK. We are not speaking about [Ollie].”.

    "Silence" 🤫An unusual response from Unai Emery 😅 pic.twitter.com/kWNZtQu3PA.

    Industry observers note that on taking charge of his first match as City head coach, Enzo Maresca told Sky Sports: “It’s big emotion. It’s a very nice feeling, the first game at home in front of our fans, so hopefully we can give them the three points.”.

    When asked about Elliot Anderson and the void left by Rodri, he added: “I think Elliot [Anderson] has to be himself; a good player, he’s going to be even better, but he has to be himself. Again, for me, there are no players that they are the same player, they are all different.

    In a recent development, “We are happy with Elliot, but for sure, as we know, Rodri is a big player but he’s already gone. So now the focus is on the ones that are here with us and the ones that will probably arrive.”.

    Recent findings suggest that brighton have spent around £100m this summer but of those only the Croatian centre-back, Luka Vušković, is in the starting XI to face Aston Villa. He cost £46m from Spurs. Brighton have, as ever, sold players with Jan-Paul Van Hecke the biggest price. The expectation is that Carlos Baleba will leave for Manchester United. He is not in the squad. The injured Yankuba Minteh would not have been involved today - but he is another likely departure. Player of the year Ferdi Kadioglu is missing with injury.

    Pep Guardiola’s successor assessed the breadth of the challenge before him and offered a candid appraisal of how to replace the irreplaceable. “It would be silly to try and change it,” he said of Guardiola’s grand design.

    According to recent reports, tito Vilanova was addressing the world’s media in Camp Nou. For Barcelona in 2012, read Manchester in 2026. Enzo Maresca would be wise to study the manual for standing on the shoulder of a giant.

    Charged with maintaining the standards of a two-time Champions League-winning team many still consider the best ever, Vilanova’s substantial idea was effectively to leave the existing one alone, mastering the art of the subtle tweak.

    Describing the transition as seamless barely does justice to the changeover; Vilanova’s Barcelona side won 23 of their first 25 La Liga matches, snatching back the title lost to Real Madrid in Guardiola’s farewell campaign. Tragically, the promise of further honours to build on sturdy foundations was realised by others as Vilanova died from cancer in 2014.

    After a brief stint by Gerardo Martino, Luis Enrique gave the dream team of Lionel Messi, Andrés Iniesta and Sergio Busquets further La Liga titles and another Champions League win.

    The so-called “impossible job” of being bound by the weight of the preceding genius, therefore, was no such thing.

    Sources indicate that the Villa team is missing six of the players who started the Europa League final against Freiburg on May 20. Four of them have left (Ezri Konsa, Morgan Rogers, Lucas Digne, Youri Tielemans) and Emi Martinez and Ollie Watkins might be leaving too - they are absent today. Belgian goalkeeper Marco Bizot starts and there is also a place for teenager George Hemmings. Emi Buendia in what looks like the central striker role. It is certainly a bracing opening day to the season for Unai Emery.

    Recent findings suggest that no sign of Watkins in what is an objectively underpowered Aston Villa line-up. There’s also no start for upcoming signing Suzuki, with Emery preferring Bizot between the sticks. Academy graduate Hemmings makes his first Premier League start.

    Some eyebrows raised at the inclusion of Rico Lewis in City’s starting XI, presumably as a defensive midfielder given the presence of Dias, Guehi, O’Reilly and Khusanov on the team-sheet. He did not have a pleasant afternoon in Cardiff last weekend, although that could be said for several City players. Some lingering doubts about his physicality, in a Premier League becoming ever more hands-on, but Enzo Maresca knows him from his time as an assistant here and clearly rates him. Wonder whether that sentiment will endure if (when) City buy some new midfielders in the coming weeks.

    🔵 TEAM NEWS🍒The first #afcb team of the latest Premier League season 👊 pic.twitter.com/uJhTI01Jld.

    Sources indicate that welcome to live coverage of Sunday afternoon’s 2pm Premier League kick-offs. Enzo Maresca faces the unenviable task of following Pep Guardiola’s decade of dominance at Manchester City and his reign begins in earnest with a visit from Bournemouth, who themselves are ushering in a new era after Marco Rose succeeded Andoni Iraola. A bruising 3-0 defeat in the Community Shield last weekend does not bode well for City’s hopes of closing the gap to Arsenal, but Maresca will be telling his charges that this afternoon is a fresh start: a new week and a new competition, plus Erling Haaland has a new haircut….

    The Italian’s squad has been shorn of World Cup winner Rodri, who departed for Barcelona this week, and the spotlight will turn to £116m club-record signing Elliot Anderson who is expected to make his Premier League debut with City. Jérémy Doku is out for two to three weeks after suffering a calf injury, which could open the door for Jack Grealish, with City bereft of wide options. City will have their work cut out as Bournemouth, fresh off a historic sixth-place finish last season, look to extend their 18-match unbeaten run from the end of last season. The Cherries won three of their five pre-season matches, which included an eye-catching 10-1 victory over Serie A side Genoa.

    According to recent reports, brighton and Hove Albion welcome Aston Villa to the Amex for their 2026-27 season opener having travelled 220 miles north of the Arctic Circle to play Norwegian side Tromso in their Europa Conference league play-off on Thursday. Fabian Hurzeler’s side face the defending Europa League champions without Carlos Baleba, who is on the brink of joining Manchester United, as well as injured wingers Kaoru Mitoma and Yankuba Minteh. While Unai Emery has lost key players in Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Ezri Konsa and Lucas Digne, the funds raised has gone towards seven signings, with Zion Suzuki, the Japan goalkeeper, in line to make his first start for Villa.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    One of the biggest benefits of the NIL era is that college basketball has more elite talent than ever, now that players are returning for bigger paychecks instead of bolting for NBA money at the first opportunity.

    That made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it. Each of the three teams features players who will be performing at the next level very soon, but the best of those might be Florida superstar Thomas Haugh.

    As our own Isaac Trotter explains, if Haugh can improve his range shooting, he won't have to wait long to hear his name called in the 2027 NBA Draft.

    When it comes to how the talent broke down by conference, it was a a pretty level playing field for the most part.

    Sources indicate that not to spoil anyting, but Arizona freshman Caleb Holt did not make the cut. He did, however, turn some heads in the Wildcats' exhibition game.

    Loyalty is an excellent quality to have in a friend or partner. It's also why we love dogs.

    It should not be quite as prevalent among college football coaches, some of whom have been undone because they did what was comfortable, not what was necessarily best for the team.

    Our own John Talty highlighted five high-profile coaches who have been loyal to a fault, making hires and personnel decisions that have come back to haunt them. One of those coaches is Mike Elko. After a shaky season from Marcel Reed in 2025, Texas A&M chose not to pursue an upgrade in the portal.

    Instead, the Aggies gave Reed a major payday, and they'll miss the College Football Playoff because of it.

    According to recent reports, look, it can happen to the best of us. Dan Lanning and Dabo Swinney wound up on the list, despite the success that those two have had throughout their careers.

    Recent findings suggest that steve Sarkisian is another coach who has fallen into the trap of being too loyal, but he may have a huge decision on his hands in the offseason. Arch Manning has struggled enough that another year in college should be on the table. If that happens, would Sark welcome back Manning with open arms, despite his shortcomings?

    In a recent development, finally, one person for whom loyalty is no an matter is Missouri QB Austin Simmons. After Trinidad Chambliss won the starting job at Ole Miss last year, Simmons didn't feel the need to stick around, but there won't be bitterness when Simmons returns to Oxford this weekend.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, it had to end that way, didn’t it?
    • Newcastle versus Liverpool became the Premier League’s most dramatic fixture when Kevin Keegan was manager here and, on the afternoon they flocked to the “cathedral on the hill” to pay tribute to the late, great superstar, we were treated to a contest that was in keeping with his narrative.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, it had to end that way, didn’t it? A last-minute goal, a sense of what might have been and a helter-skelter contest that will take days to decipher.

    Newcastle versus Liverpool became the Premier League’s most dramatic fixture when Kevin Keegan was manager here and, on the afternoon they flocked to the “cathedral on the hill” to pay tribute to the late, great superstar, we were treated to a contest that was in keeping with his narrative.

    Liverpool operating with the discipline of a basketball team undoubtedly helped, and we can examine those gaping chasms soon enough, but the poignancy of seeing Matthias Jaissle looking as bereft as Keegan at Anfield 30 years ago at the final whistle was impossible to ignore.

    Industry observers note that really, the German’s first match in charge of Newcastle should have ended with three points. His team are a work in progress – rich in youthful exuberance though prone to lapses – but how they fought, ran and worked to give the locals the result they wanted.

    According to recent reports, they were almost at the finish line, seconds away from beating Liverpool here for the first time since December 2015, but then Lewis Hall ran into Victor Muñoz, sending the Spanish substitute sprawling, and Stuart Attwell pointed to the penalty spot. Dominik Szoboszlai inflicted maximum damage.

    Dominik Szoboszlai equalises from the spot in the 99th minute! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/0Ag9WitqHt.

    Recent findings suggest that “I have clear thoughts,” Jaissle said quietly, as he was asked to reflect on the day-wrecking decision. “I guess you call it a soft penalty here. If you give it, you need to give a lot during this match and a lot during the season. I don’t know if it that is good for football.”.

    Here was the third time in four seasons Liverpool had scored in injury time in front of the Leazes Stand, after Darwin Núñez (2023) and Rio Ngumoha (2025), and their eighth goal beyond the 90th minute in collisions with Newcastle is a Premier League record against the same opponents.

    No wonder he was stunned. Jaissle had spent idle moments in the build-up thinking about what might happen if Newcastle scored an early goal and, much to his delight, fantasy became reality in the most thrilling fashion. On this emotional afternoon, it was fitting the hosts scored first.

    It has been revealed that one of Keegan’s great early wins as Newcastle manager was in November 1993, when his team blew away Liverpool in the snow and Andy Cole scored a first-half hat-trick. His first goal that day came after five minutes and, by happy coincidence, the clock stopped at that moment for Anthony Elanga, too.

    How Liverpool went from having a chance of their own to conceding 20 seconds later is something Andoni Iraola will have to address promptly, but that is what happened: Ryan Gravenberch should have shot, instead he passed and Amar Dedic intervened, his interception finding Will Osula.

    In a recent development, off Osula galloped, Liverpool’s defenders looking leaden-footed as they gave pursuit, and he ushered Elanga into open space. Once he was in the clear, he was not for catching and his shot was perfectly placed beyond Alisson Becker.

    According to recent reports, an electric start! Anthony Elanga gives Newcastle the lead inside 5 minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/8DYYFJ9i6F.

    As Elanga was mobbed, the recriminations started. Fingers pointed at each other, Iraola spun around in dismay. Liverpool were easy to play against last season – Iraola’s Bournemouth had scored two identical goals against them on the opening day 12 months ago – and old habits die hard.

    “We should finish the play,” Iraola conceded. “We created a great chance. We are on the edge of the box and have a clear opening to shoot and we decide not to. We don’t finish it properly and then you have to give credit to Elanga, who wins the race.”.

    Sources indicate that what could Liverpool offer in response? The answer before the interval was nothing, other than a shot from Florian Wirtz that was well saved by Lukas Hornicek. The first half was wretched and it was difficult to see what had changed from the final throes of Arne Slot.

    This, to be clear, is no criticism of Iraola, more a spotlight on players who need to step up. They did that momentarily in the second period, when Cody Gakpo equalised. He was afforded too much time by Newcastle’s defence but, still, his finish from 20 yards was super, zipping beyond Hornicek.

    Cody Gakpo with a fine finish to equalise for Liverpool! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/cfDQWbES2v.

    But parity was secured for less than two minutes before Newcastle scored a near-carbon-copy second goal, another counter-attack – this was one led by the outstanding Yoane Wissa – ending with substitute Joe Willock finding a corner of Alisson’s net. Again the inquests followed.

    "Wow!"Joe Willock restores Newcastle's advantage almost instantly with an exceptional finish! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/8IKPUgqapK.

    “We had the numbers to defend it better,” Iraola stated. “It’s not like they caught us by surprise, but we didn’t defend it properly. We should compete for the first ball and probably make a foul, be a little more aggressive as we had the numbers to defend it.

    “You don’t want to concede transitions and we’d been preparing them in the week for transitions.”.

    Why they didn’t follow the proposal that had been set is something that Iraola must address, but he will be relieved that the days spent this week are not dissecting a defeat, as Wissa should have wrapped up the contest, only for Alisson to make a brilliant save to thwart the Congolese striker.

    Recent findings suggest that those missed chances should not have mattered but in the final throes, Hall misjudged the angle Muñoz attacked him from, he got his challenge wrong and, after a pause, Attwell pointed to the spot. Given the agony Liverpool have inflicted, the outcome was as clear as black and white.

    “We scored at the end, so you have a better taste,” Iraola said. “Before the game, we wouldn’t have signed for this result. It’s a reward. It’s only a point, but at least it’s something that’s deserved.”.

    Plenty would contest his conclusion. Liverpool got away with it – and Iraola is about to find the hard work is only just beginning.

    In a recent development, you can't make the playoffs in 10 games, but you can definitely give yourself some breathing room when the inevitable ebbs and flows of the season strike. That's exactly what the Boston Bruins have done as they've stood out for the right reasons in a deep Atlantic Division.

    Boston currently leads the division with 15 points, and while the Tampa Bay Lightning's record is technically better, the Bruins' plus-14 goal differential is tied for second in the NHL.

    The biggest reason for this fast start has been the play of Jeremy Swayman in goal. He's allowed one or fewer goals in half of his starts, and Swayman's 8.02 goals saved above average ranks second to old Beantown running mate Linus Ullmark, per Natural Stat Trick.

    We have a long way to go before we start discussing Vezina Trophy candidates seriously, but Swayman certainly has the potential to carry Boston to the postseason.

    It helps that David Pastrnak is an elite playmaker, and the Bruins have been getting contributions from young forwards Fraser Minten and James Hagens. Morgan Geekie has also gone from goal-scoring machine to distributor with seven assists in 10 games.

    Industry observers note that the Atlantic Division will be a heavyweight brawl throughout the season, but to this point, the Bruins have proven to be a worthy combatant. With that in mind, here are the updated NHL Power Rankings.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Week 12 of the NFL season kicks off with a rare Wednesday matchup between the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams, prepping us for a full Thanksgiving feast of football the following day, headlined by an MVP showcase between the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs on Thursday night.

    In a recent development, we're watching plenty of injuries ahead of the action, including Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III, who's missed the last two games with a groin injury suffered in practice. He was officially limited on Tuesday. Fantasy football managers will also be keeping a Las Vegas Raiders All-Pro tight end Brock Bowers, who missed Week 11 with an ankle injury, though he was reportedly pushing to play in that matchup.

    In a recent development, the week also saw two players hit free agency after clearing waivers, including former Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones and former San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk. Aiyuk reportedly has a visit scheduled with the Washington Commanders on Wednesday, who are short on receiver help after a season-ending knee injury to Terry McLaurin, while Jones' future remains up in the air.

    Follow along with Yahoo Sports for the latest NFL news, injury updates and more coming out of Week 11.

    The Eagles listed star running back Saquon Barkley as a full practice participant on Tuesday.

    The injury report did note that it was just a walkthrough, but yesterday, when Philly did not practice, the team listed Barkley as a limited practice participant due to a neck injury as well as an illness.

    The Eagles play the Cowboys on Thursday afternoon for Thanksgiving.

    Brandon Aiyuk may have a newly introduced home sooner than later.

    It has been revealed that the former 49ers receiver is scheduled to visit with the Washington Commanders. That's according to his agent, Drew Rosenhaus, who told ESPN's Adam Schefter that Aiyuk will meet with the Commanders on Wednesday.

    Ayiuk cleared waivers on Tuesday after previously being released by the 49ers, concluding a protracted and contentious breakup with the franchise.

    After finally being released by the San Francisco 49ers, veteran wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk has cleared waivers, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter, who also reported Tuesday that Aiyuk would like to sign with a newly introduced team soon.

    He's expected to attract interest from a few teams, including the Washington Commanders, per Schefter.

    The Niners releasing Aiyuk marked the end of a months-long standoff between the team and player. Aiyuk missed the entire 2025 NFL season after recovering from a knee injury he suffered in 2024, just months after signing a four-year, $120 million extension with the team. He suffered a torn ACL and MCL in late October 2024 and hasn't played a snap in the league since.

    San Francisco had a two-week roster exemption for Aiyuk. It expired on Monday, and as a result, the franchise opted to release Aiyuk, giving both the team and the wide receiver a fresh start.

    According to recent reports, denver Broncos running back J.K. Dobbins has been suspended for one game for conduct detrimental to the team, according to head coach Sean Payton.

    Payton did not get into specifics and told reporters he would not comment further on the situation.

    In a recent development, dobbins, 27, is in his second season with the Broncos. He has rushed for 324 yards and 3 touchdowns on 99 carries, adding 31 receiving yards on 9 catches. Last year, Dobbins compiled 772 rushing yards and 4 TDs.

    Recent findings suggest that the suspension leaves Denver will be without its leading rusher for Friday's Week 12 matchup with the Pittsburgh Steelers. Jonah Coleman (302 rushing yards in 6 games) will presumably take over as the starter.

    Micah Parsons is officially activated off the Physically Unable to Perform list, Green Bay Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst revealed on Tuesday.

    Sources indicate that so the All-Pro pass rusher appears to be ready to play in Wednesday's Thanksgiving Eve matchup versus the Los Angeles Rams. Parsons had been listed as questionable for the game.

    Parsons has been sidelined while recovering from a torn ACL and meniscus suffered during Week 15 last season. Prior to his injury, he compiled 12.5 sacks in 14 games (13 starts) in his first year with Green Bay.

    While Green Bay Packers edge rusher Micah Parsons is reportedly poised to make his long-awaited return from his ACL injury Wednesday night against the Los Angeles Rams, he's officially listed as "questionable" for the Week 12 matchup.

    In Parsons' first, abridged season with the Packers, he piled up 12.5 sacks over 14 games.

    Running back Josh Jacobs is also "questionable" for the Thanksgiving Eve game at SoFi Stadium.

    He's been recovering from surgery on the ring finger he fractured.

    The Kansas City Chiefs have been cautious handling the groin injury that running back Kenneth Walker III is navigating.

    Walker hasn't played since Nov. 8, a Week 9 win over the New York Jets.

    Chiefs head coach Andy Reid told reporters that Walker will return to practice Tuesday.

    "We'll see how he does," Reid noted, per Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star. "I'm not anticipating a ton of work there, but he'll get out there and move around.".

    The Chiefs will travel to Buffalo this week for a Thanksgiving showdown with the Bills.

    If there's anything that can slow this 49ers team, it's the blue medical tent. Injuries have ravaged the 49ers all season, and on Sunday night, San Francisco ran out a Geriatric Avengers of thirty-somethings including George Kittle, Mike Evans, Christian McCaffrey, Deebo Samuel Sr. and Kyle Juszczyk. All that experience gives the 49ers a big-game-pressure edge that few teams can match, but it also makes them intensely vulnerable to injury. Stints on the IR are a when, not an if, for the 49ers. Right tackle Colton McKivitz was the latest as he suffered a gruesome leg injury in the first half Sunday night.

    In a recent development, the guy ensuring all those uncs get the ball is finally receiving some attention of his own again, too. Brock Purdy hasn't shown up on MVP leaderboards since finishing fourth in his breakout season of 2023. This season ought to change that. He's among the league leaders in touchdowns, passer rating and completion percentage, among other useful stats.

    Against the best defense in the NFL, all Purdy did was throw for three touchdowns and 255 yards on 21-of-26 completions. He's grown into the perfect weapon for head coach Kyle Shanahan's unorthodox offense, and Sunday was the perfect showcase.

    McCarthy was asked on Monday whether he was considering a quarterback change after the offense's poor play in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.

    McCarthy kept it short and to the point, saying, "Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback.".

    Pittsburgh dropped to 6-4 after the loss and fell to third place in the AFC North, trailing both the Cincinnati Bengals and the Cleveland Browns.

    The Steelers had 255 yards of offense but couldn't beat the Eagles. Philadelphia's win ended a seven-game losing streak for the franchise, and the Steelers have now lost two straight games, both coming after their Week 9 bye.

    In the loss, Rodgers was 30-of-44 passing for 227 yards and a touchdown. He led the team in rushing with 29 yards on five carries, but was sacked five times.

    If the Latest England Patriots are interested in adding quarterback Daniel Jones, head coach Mike Vrabel isn't saying so.

    While Jones has cleared waivers, the Patriots named Tommy DeVito as their starting QB for Week 12's matchup with the Los Angeles Chargers. However, even if Upcoming England signed Jones, he would be unlikely to take the field with them so soon after joining the team.

    Sources indicate that taking over after Drake Maye was injured in Week 10's game versus the Detroit Lions, DeVito completed 12-of-24 passes for 81 yards with 1 touchdown and 1 interception. Vrabel stated he was impressed by the backup QB's performance and the improvement he's shown since training camp, even if the Patriots didn't win the game.

    The plan is for Sam Darnold to start against the 49ers on Sunday, but Mike Macdonald wants to see the quarterback in practice first before making a final decision.

    Darnold has been out for two games due to a quad injury suffered in Week 8.

    Before Week 11, the Fresh York Giants had a perception problem.

    They hadn't beaten a team with a winning record. Their advanced metrics remarked they were a below-average team. Their point differential was +7, which was meager for a 5-3-1 team. They looked like a team lucky to be playing in the putrid NFC East.

    It has been revealed that then on Sunday, the Giants got a win that can help legitimize their start. They beat a Jaguars team that was a major buyer at the trade deadline and looked like one of the NFL's elite teams. It was easily the Giants' biggest win this season, and for a team that has missed the playoffs eight of the past nine seasons, one of their biggest victories in many years. It might change what is being remarked about the Giants.

    Industry observers note that "We don't really worry about that, we don't really care what they think or what they say," Giants head coach John Harbaugh remarked after the game, via the team's transcripts. "It's not our concern how we're evaluated. It's our concern how we play.".

    Yet, they knew what was being said about them.

    Industry observers note that after missing nearly a year with tears to his ACL and meniscus, Micah Parsons is set to return to the Packers' defensive line this week. The star linebacker has reportedly been cleared to play as of Monday, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

    Parsons reportedly needed one final clearance on his knee before getting the green light, and will now make his debut against the Rams on Wednesday.

    Fresh York Giants cornerback Greg Newsome will be sidelined for "multiple weeks" with a high ankle sprain, head coach John Harbaugh confirmed on Monday.

    It's still unclear if Newsome will need surgery or if he will land on injured reserve, which would knock him out for at least four games.

    "It's a serious high ankle. It's gonna be one of those lengthy high ankles," Harbaugh noted, via ESPN. "It's going to be multiple weeks.".

    For more on Newsome's injury, click here.

    San Francisco is finally parting ways with wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk.

    After a months-long saga around the receiver wanting to be released, Aiyuk was officially waived by the 49ers on Monday. That confirms reports earlier on Monday indicating that Aiyuk would finally be released.

    Other teams will have until Wednesday to claim Aiyuk, who will become a free agent after he clears waivers.

    Former Colts quarterback Daniel Jones was not claimed on Monday, thus making him a free agent.

    Jones is free to sign with any team that wants him, and that team can pay him the veteran minimum.

    The Colts still owe Jones about $20 million.

    The Commanders have activated running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt from injured reserve, and he is off the injury report.

    According to recent reports, JCM will play Monday night against the Bengals. He hasn't played since Week 5 due to a groin injury.

    In a recent development, so far this season, Croskey-Merritt has 239 yards and two touchdowns on 67 carries. He also has 40 yards on five receptions.

    The Cardinals have reportedly fired defensive coordinator Nick Rallis, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

    Sources indicate that arizona's defense has allowed 355.2 yards per game this season, the seventh-most in the league. The Cardinals' allowing 29.4 points per game is the second-most in the league, trailing only the Raiders at 29.7 points per game.

    San Francisco 49ers general manager John Lynch has agreed to a multi-year contract extension with the team, according to reports.

    Lynch and team owner Jed York agreed to the newly introduced contract with a handshake while on the sideline at Estadio Banorte before Sunday night's 35-10 win over the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City, Fox Sports' Jay Glazer reported.

    Exact terms of Lynch's extension have not yet been reported. The 49ers have not officially unveiled the agreement. Lynch's current contract was set to expire after this season.

    According to recent reports, lynch's newly introduced deal joins an extension for head coach Kyle Shanahan, who reached agreement on the contract in September shortly after the 49ers played the Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne, Australia. San Francisco's international games this season have been extremely lucrative for the team's top football authority figures.

    Rams head coach Sean McVay said Monday that tight end Terrance Ferguson will need season-ending surgery on his ankle.

    Industry observers note that ferguson is the latest Rams player to be dealing with a long-term injury. Wide receiver Puka Nacua will also miss the remainder of the season due to a knee injury. Davante Adams has been sidelined since Week 6, though he is expected back by mid-December.

    Ferguson's season ends with him playing in just three games. He finished with 63 yards and a touchdown on seven receptions.

    #108428. Industry News: Connor Hellebuyck trade: Jets send star goalie to the Devils in exchange for four players, two draft picks

    📅 24 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1163 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Connor Hellebuyck trade: Jets send star goalie to the Devils in exchange for four players, two draft picks

    📅 24 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1163 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that connor Hellebuyck is a now a Devil.
    • Industry observers note that hellebuyck expressed his desire to be traded in the offseason when he formally requested a move in August.
    • Hellebuyck has spent his entire career with Winnipeg after being drafted by the Jets in 2012 at No.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that connor Hellebuyck is a now a Devil. The star goalie for the Winnipeg Jets is on the move after being traded to New Jersey on Friday in exchange for four players and two future draft picks. the teams announced the move with the Jets receiving Dawson Mercer, Nick Bjugstad, Nico Daws and Alexander Command, plus a 2027 seventh-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick.

    Industry observers note that hellebuyck expressed his desire to be traded in the offseason when he formally requested a move in August. He said at the time that he had made the request months earlier and tried to keep the situation private.

    Hellebuyck has spent his entire career with Winnipeg after being drafted by the Jets in 2012 at No. 130 overall. He's recognized as one of the best goalies in the league as a three-time Vezina Trophy winner. He also helped carry the United States to its first gold medal since 1980 at the 2026 Olympics in February with some incredible saves against Canada in the final game.

    After trading Jacob Markstom in the offseason, the Devils had a clear need in goal, and this splashy move certainly fills that need. With a talented young core already in place, Latest Jersey's Stanley Cup window is wide open.

    RAISE HELLE!Connor Hellebuyck is a Newly introduced Jersey Devil: https://t.co/HCehRGOQI5 pic.twitter.com/dZGNQR16m1.

    In a recent development, for the Jets, it must be a hard pill to swallow when a franchise icon decides to walk out they door, but this trade package should help them as the enter a new era and revamp the roster. Winnipeg got a former first-rounder in Mercer to try and add to a rebuild as well as a veteran presence in Bjugstad. They also acquired a younger goalie in Daws who could fill the role of Hellebuyck at just 25 years old.

    Recent findings suggest that goaltending has been an glitch in Newly introduced Jersey for a while now -- even after the team acquired Markstrom from the Calgary Flames in 2024. Markstom never really panned out, and his 13.6 goals allowed above average, per Natural Stat Trick, were a major reason why the Devils missed the postseason last year.

    According to recent reports, in the early portion of this season, it was clear that New Jersey needed to make a move to upgrade in the crease. Daws and veteran Jake Allen simply aren't a tandem suitable for a Stanley Cup contender, and the numbers backed that up. New Jersey ranks 24th in team save percentage at .877, and the duo of Daws and Allen combined to surrender 2.99 goals above average.

    Once Hellebuyck gets up to game speed, that shouldn't be a problem anymore.

    In a recent development, in the three-season stretch from 2023-26, Hellebuyck led the NHL with 73.42 goals saved above average, which is 20 goals higher than the next closest netminder. Over that span, Hellebuyck also posted a standard save percentage of .914 and an astronomical high-danger save-percentage of .832.

    Hellebuyck carried less talented teams to the playoffs multiple times in his career. Now on a team loaded with weaponry in their prime -- Jack Hughes, Jesper Bratt and Nico Hischier to name a few -- Hellebuyck could be the final piece to the championship puzzle.

    In a recent development, in terms of the acquisition cost, it was probably an easy deal for Devils general manager Sunny Mehta to make. The 2029 second-round pick is useless for a team that should be all-in now, Bjugstad is simply a depth piece and Daws now has no path to a starting role with Hellebuyck in town.

    Industry observers note that the most interesting trade chips are Mercer and Command. Mercer flashed major upside with 56 points in his second NHL season, 2022-23, but he hasn't really come close to hitting those heights again. Still, even if he has plateaued, Mercer remains a strong middle-six forward rising into his prime.

    In a recent development, although Command had his detractors -- and may have been over-drafted at No. 12 overall -- he was a consensus first-round pick last summer. That gives Winnipeg a potential franchise forward it can build around long-term, but New Jersey already has one of the deepest forward groups in the league, especially with the emergence of Arseny Gritsyuk and the acquisition of Luke Evangelista.

    Recent findings suggest that if we're looking for a 3-D chess angle of this deal, it only makes the Devils more appealing for a certain Minnesota Wild defenseman whose brothers just happen to play in Newly introduced Jersey already. Grade -- A+.

    Let's get the obvious out of the way first: The Jets were never going to get fair value for Hellebuyck because, at his best, he's the No. 1 goaltender in the world with no equal. That type of excellence can't be replaced.

    Recent findings suggest that that said, Winnipeg did fairly well given the circumstances. Hellebuyck made a public trade request, and he wasn't even with the team after sitting out for the entirety of training camp. The entire league knew the Jets had to trade him.

    Hellebuyck's talent created a decent market anyway, but most of the suitors were bona fide Stanley Cup contenders with little in the way of valuable draft capital, and they weren't going to knee cap the roster by sending a key player back in return.

    It has been revealed that with all that taken into consideration, Kevin Cheveldayoff got a solid return. Although Mercer's ceiling may be lower than initially thought, he's a 24-year-old forward who banks roughly 20 goals and 20 assists every season. The kicker with Mercer will be Winnipeg's ability to re-sign him before he hits restricted free agency next summer.

    The addition of Command means Winnipeg now has two forwards selected in the top 12 of the 2026 NHL Draft after taking center Viggo Bjorck themselves. If both of those players deliver on their first-round pedigrees, they could be a terrific one-two punch for the team long-term.

    According to recent reports, daws was a third-round pick in 2020, and despite playing just 13 NHL games since the start of the 2024-25 season, he should give Winnipeg a solid back up option behind Stuart Skinner. It certainly helps that Skinner is off to a great start with his newly introduced team -- and if Daws develops into a true No. 1 -- it'll be gravy.

    Sources indicate that if there's any reason to critique this deal from the Jets' side of things, it's that they didn't get premium draft capital or a surefire up-and-coming prospect. Maybe Command develops into a star, but there's no guarantee he becomes a top-six stud in the NHL.

    The Jets got a lot of good stuff, but they didn't really get anything great, at least not based on what we know in the moment. Because of that, I have to ding Winnipeg a little bit. Grade: B.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Joel Embiid is listed as doubtful due to illness for Wednesday's NBA Cup matchup between the Philadelphia 76ers and Miami Heat.

    In a recent development, embiid also missed Monday's 128-111 loss to the Portland Trail Blazers. The Sixers center will have missed five of the team's 18 games this season.

    Recent findings suggest that prior to Monday, he had appeared in Philadelphia's past three games and played arguably his best basketball of the season, averaging 30 points. That stretch includes Saturday's 132-129 win over the Milwaukee Bucks during which he nearly notched a triple-double with 26 points, 17 rebounds and 9 assists.

    Embiid was involved in a crucial play in the closing seconds, taking an inbounds pass from LeBron James and stepping out of bounds at the baseline. However, the officials failed to notice Embiid's left foot going out and the Bucks were out of replay challenges to contest the call.

    Sources indicate that embiid is the 76ers' third-leading scorer at 20.4 points per game while leading the team with 8.9 rebounds. His 4.1 assists rank fourth among Sixers players.

    In a recent development, the 76ers currently have the top record in the Eastern Conference at 14-4 and are tied for second in the NBA behind the 15-3 San Antonio Spurs and Los Angeles Lakers. Philadelphia has won seven of its past 10 games.

    Following Wednesday's contest, the Sixers have back-to-back games on the road, visiting the Indiana Pacers (6-12) on Friday and facing the Houston Rockets (13-5) on Saturday.

    Embiid seems likely to miss at least one of those games, if not for illness than perhaps the right foot plantar fascia management that has sidelined him for a game when the Sixers play a back-to-back.

    Latest Update: What it's really like to kill a fellow athlete - and the terrible grief 'you carry for the rest of your life': The cursed band of haunted sportsmen reveal the nightmares that never leave them
