    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Published: 21:00 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 22:15 EST, 19 November 2026.
    • Towards the end of the Australian summer of 2014-15, as the country prepared to host the Cricket World Cup, I took a flight from Sydney to Hobart, Tasmania, to watch a Sheffield Shield game between Tasmania and Fresh South Wales at the Bellerive Oval, a beautiful ground perched on the banks of the Derwent River.
    • It has been revealed that australian sport was still in shock.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By OLIVER HOLT, CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

    Published: 21:00 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 22:15 EST, 19 November 2026.

    Towards the end of the Australian summer of 2014-15, as the country prepared to host the Cricket World Cup, I took a flight from Sydney to Hobart, Tasmania, to watch a Sheffield Shield game between Tasmania and Fresh South Wales at the Bellerive Oval, a beautiful ground perched on the banks of the Derwent River.

    It has been revealed that australian sport was still in shock. A few months earlier, Australia's Test opener, Phillip Hughes, had died after he was struck on the side of his neck by a short ball from a young bowler called Sean Abbott in a game between Upcoming South Wales and South Australia at the Sydney Cricket Ground.

    Hughes was treated at the ground for 40 minutes and then taken by ambulance to St Vincent's Hospital in nearby Darlinghurst in a critical condition. 'Feeling for Phil Hughes after being hit,' former Australia Test cricketer Dean Jones wrote on Twitter. 'He is not in a good way! Stay strong Sean Abbott. Not your fault, young man.'.

    It has been revealed that the impact of the ball had compressed a vein in Hughes' neck and when it split, it caused a catastrophic bleed on the brain. Hughes had emergency surgery and was placed in an induced coma. He never regained consciousness and passed away two days later.

    Recent findings suggest that hughes was a popular, talented, gutsy cricketer with three Test centuries already under his belt. A small guy with the heart of a lion. He was 25 years old. Cricket mourned a terrible tragedy – some called it the sport's saddest day and the agony of Hughes' family was hard to bear. But there was something else. There was an awareness that two tragedies were playing out in front of us.

    Hughes was lost but the man who had bowled the delivery that felled him had been left behind, desolate and distraught. Many thought Sean Abbott, who was 22, would never play cricket again. That he would not be able to find the strength. But that was why I had flown to Tasmania. Because Abbott had found the strength.

    Phil Hughes was the golden boy of Australian cricket in 2014, with three Test centuries already to his name, when he was hit by a ball bowled by Sean Abbott and died.

    Abbott visiting the Sydney hospital where Hughes was in a coma that he would never wake from, having suffered a catastrophic bleed on the brain.

    According to recent reports, that February afternoon at the Bellerive Oval, I sat among a smattering of spectators who watched Abbott walk to the top of his mark. His team-mates shouted encouragement to him. They were willing him on with everything they had and Abbott bowled his heart out.

    Industry observers note that 'Beautifully bowled, Abbo,' one of the NSW fielders shouted after one ball to former Test opener Ed Cowan. 'That's a beauty, Seanie,' another yelled after the fifth ball of his first over, when Cowan jerked his head out of the way of a short delivery so fast he fell over. Only one wicket fell that afternoon. Abbott took it.

    According to recent reports, it was one of the bravest sporting performances I have ever witnessed. Because even though cricket had voiced its support for Abbott, the sport could not protect him from his thoughts and from the knowledge he had become one of a cursed band of sportsmen who have unwittingly caused the death of an opponent during a contest.

    It has been revealed that sometimes, tragedy in sport is not just the tragedy of the player who dies; it is the tragedy of the opponent who must live the nightmare of what he has done over and over again in his mind. To those that it has befallen, they say it is a grief that never leaves them.

    That grief, that sense of a double tragedy, was brought sharply back into focus earlier this month when Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel died in hospital the day after a sickening collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono. The accident happened in the final minutes of a game in Spain's Segunda Division, when Owono hurtled out of his goal and collided with De Miguel in the centre circle. He was shown a red card for the foul.

    There was an outpouring of grief for De Miguel. I was among those who observed a minute's silence for him before the Barcelona-Aston Villa Champions League tie at the Nou Camp the next evening. Tributes continue to be paid to him. Owono, meanwhile, has become a pariah. It is mentioned that the 25-year-old rarely leaves his house.

    According to recent reports, owono does not appear to have had the same sympathy extended to him that Abbott benefited from. His challenge on De Miguel, a striker who had had a peripatetic career in Spain's lower leagues, was reckless and cavalier. For him, the struggle with guilt and responsibility and public judgment is only just beginning.

    FC Andorra will play their first home game since the tragedy against Leganes on Friday night but when they run out at the Encamp Stadium, a neat little ground beside a babbling river, the Valira d'Orient, and in the shadow of the mountains that make Andorra such a popular ski resort, Owono will not be there.

    Earlier this month Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel died in hospital the day after a sickening collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono.

    According to recent reports, owono has become a pariah. It is stated that the 25-year-old rarely leaves his house.

    The goalkeeper, who has 47 caps for Equatorial Guinea, was given the maximum sentence of a 12-match ban by the Spanish Football Federation.

    Tenerife manager Alvaro Cervera suggested Owono's ban 'might feel light' to all those mourning the striker, who was 30 years old, while FC Andorra owner Gerard Pique, the former Barcelona and Spain centre back, stated the maximum sanction 'puts him (Owono) in a situation he does not deserve, because he is not to blame for all of this having happened'.

    No one knows whether Owono will feel able to return to football when his ban ends. Footage circulated of him in an on-field argument moments before the clash with De Miguel, and it was used to suggest that he was in an unstable state of mind.

    Industry observers note that some have pressed for him to be charged with manslaughter. His Instagram account was deactivated after it was deluged with abuse, including messages which branded him 'a murderer'. It has been reported that his brother, who is also a footballer, has been the victim of abuse because of his association with Owono.

    Owono has only communicated through a statement released by his club. 'These are the most difficult days of my life,' he wrote. 'I struggle to find the words, and I find it very hard to ​process what has happened. I feel enormous pain at the loss of Jesus. I think of him, his family, and all the people who loved him. I know there will be many questions to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect.'.

    I spoke to the great British fighter Barry McGuigan about Owono this week. McGuigan has suffered his share of tragedies. His brother, Dermot, took his own life. He lost his daughter, Danika, to cancer when she was just 33, in 2019. And in 1982, three years before he won the world featherweight title at Loftus Road, he nearly quit boxing altogether.

    According to recent reports, in the 12th fight of his professional career, McGuigan fought a Nigerian boxer called Young Ali at the World Sporting Club in Mayfair. He still remembers the clink of cutlery coming from the diners who were sitting ringside that night. That sound still takes him back.

    McGuigan still remembers the sequence of punches that put Young Ali down in the sixth round of the fight. He saw his opponent's eyes roll back in his head and a feeling of dread washed over him. Young Ali, just 21, fell into a coma from which he never emerged and died five months later.

    I spoke to the great British fighter Barry McGuigan (right) about Owono this week. McGuigan has suffered his share of tragedies.

    Sources indicate that 'There was the horror of that and we sat and we waited and we prayed that he would be better and he never got better,' McGuigan told me. 'I didn't know whether I wanted to continue boxing. I thought: "If I can do this to somebody…"'.

    According to recent reports, he shuddered when he talked about Owono. 'Other tragedies happen and other terrible things happen,' he said. 'Life is a struggle. Something like that, you never leave it behind you.

    'It is something invisible and it depends how emotionally vulnerable he is. He may never be the same again but I hope he is able to overcome it.'.

    There are others out there in sport, still trying to overcome it. Think of Matt Petgrave, the Sheffield Steelers ice-hockey player who was arrested on suspicion of manslaughter after his skate fatally cut the neck of Nottingham Panthers' Adam Johnson in an Elite Ice Hockey League match at Sheffield Arena in October 2023.

    Industry observers note that think of Jochen Mass, the Formula One driver, who spent years blaming himself for the death of Gilles Villeneuve during qualifying for the Belgian Grand Prix at Zolder in 1982, because he slowed and moved to the right in front of Villeneuve. The Ferrari ran into the back of Mass and flipped in grotesque cartwheels across the track.

    Think of Matthias Behr, the German fencer who killed his opponent, Vladimir Smirnov, at the 1982 World Fencing Championships in Rome when Behr's foil blade broke during a match, penetrated the Ukrainian fencer's mask and pierced his eye.

    Think of Gary Cully, the Irish fighter, who learned this week that his last opponent, Lee Reeves, had died after spending three months in a coma following their bout in Dublin in August.

    'What a character and a gent,' Cully wrote in tribute to Reeves. 'It's never been nothing but love between us champ, can't really believe I'm writing this but RIP brother.'.

    Nottingham Panthers' Adam Johnson died in October 2023 when opponent Matt Petgrave's skate cut his neck during a match.

    Gary Cully (left), the Irish fighter, learned this week that his last opponent, Lee Reeves (right), had died after spending three months in a coma following their bout in Dublin in August.

    Dr Victor Thompson, a prominent UK clinical sports psychologist, has studied the effect on competitors of being involved in the death of a rival.

    'The biggest thing a player will have had to absorb normally is bad performance,' Dr Thompson claims. 'Now he has to absorb the fact that he was involved in somebody dying. He will be trying to work out was it his fault? Is he to blame? And all of that, because the emotions are so high, gets associated with playing the sport in question.

    'So when Sean Abbott thought about going out there again, when he thought about putting his pads on, or putting his kit on and being around team-mates or the smell of the cricket bat – it'll all be associated to that very traumatic day.'.

    In a recent development, university of North Carolina academic John M Silva III argued that aggression in sport is defined in two categories: hostile aggression and instrumental aggression. Hostile is when the main aim is to cause harm or injury to your opponent. Instrumental is aggression for a purpose, perhaps ball recovery or to sow doubt in an opponent’s mind.

    The interpretation of a player's actions at a time of high stress, frustration or adversarial combat is often central to the reaction to a sporting tragedy. Whether forgiveness is extended to or opprobrium visited on the competitor who has caused the death of another.

    In a recent development, that interpretation was used against Petgrave, who was notorious for having a bad disciplinary record on the ice. Some likened the action which fatally injured Johnson to a kung-fu kick and drew a link between it and some of his past behaviour. He was mercilessly trolled on social media. Team-mates, and many ice hockey fans, leapt to his defence and stated any suggestion his action was deliberate was fanciful. They said his unusual action in lifting his left skate high was a direct result of being knocked off balance by a collision.

    Sources indicate that petgrave could not return to ice hockey immediately even if he had wanted to. It was a full 18 months before the Crown Prosecution Service and South Yorkshire Police decided there was no realistic prospect of conviction for manslaughter and that no criminal charges should be brought against the 34-year-old Canadian.

    In the intervening period, Petgrave's family set up a crowdfunding page, pointing out that he was unable to work or to return home until the CPS had decided whether to press charges. The page raised nearly £20,000 from well-wishers.

    The interpretation of a player's actions at a time of high stress, frustration or adversarial combat is often central to the reaction to a sporting tragedy - as it was for Petgrave.

    Petgrave did receive widespread support from inside his sport, with a standing ovation at his Sheffield side's next home match, while he was beginning 18 months under investigation.

    'This has been the most painful and overwhelming period of our lives,' a message from Petgrave's family noted at the bottom of the page. 'Watching someone I love go through this has been incredibly difficult.

    'Despite everything, we are doing our best to stay strong, and the support and kindness from so many people have been a source of strength. We continue to recognise the heartbreaking nature of this situation, and our thoughts remain with everyone affected. We hold on to hope that this will soon come to an end.'.

    It has been revealed that petgrave now plies his trade in the minor league ECHL for the Indy Fuel, a team based in Fishers, Indiana. He is an ever-present this season, playing opponents like the Wheeling Nailers, the Greenville Swamp Rabbits, the Kalamazoo Wings and the Bloomington Bison.

    'We understand the responsibility that comes with the great support we receive from this community,' Sean Hallett, CEO of Hallett Sports, which owns the Fuel, said when they hired Petgrave. 'We are confident he will be a positive addition to our team and our city.'.

    I wrote to the Fuel, asking if there was any chance of speaking to Petgrave. They did not respond. The reticence is understandable and, in many ways, laudable. Players involved in this kind of tragedy are preoccupied with respect for the victims' families and the sensitivities that come with such terrible grief. There is nothing they can say or do to make it better.

    Sometimes, it is the other way round. Sometimes, it is the family of a lost loved one who find a way to ease the pain of a sportsman eaten up by shame for inadvertently causing the death of a competitor.

    Mass, who died last year, blamed himself for the sickening crash that killed the most exciting, charismatic, talented, electrifying driver in Formula One. As Villeneuve's Ferrari cartwheeled across the track, breaking into pieces, he was flung clear of the wreckage still strapped to his seat, catapulting across the track until he came to rest in the catch-fencing by the side of the circuit. He died of catastrophic injuries later that evening, aged 32.

    Mass was absolved of responsibility. It was a tragic accident. Villeneuve was running hot after a disagreement with his team-mate Didier Pironi and was pushing even his own boundaries. There were any number of extenuating circumstances but Mass still blamed himself. He retired from the sport the same season.

    As Gilles Villeneuve's Ferrari cartwheeled across the track, breaking into pieces, he was flung clear of the wreckage still strapped to his seat, catapulting across the track.

    Despite being absolved of responsibility, Jochen Mass (pictured in 2019) blamed himself for the accident and retired from the sport the same year.

    It was years later when he felt a tap on the shoulder as he was sitting on a plane. He looked up to see Villeneuve's son, Jacques, the 1997 F1 world champion, standing over him.

    According to recent reports, 'I felt so guilty about what had happened and then suddenly, there was Jacques,' Mass recalled. 'He mentioned: "Jochen, our family – we never blamed you. It was a racing incident – just a wrong decision by the two of you."'.

    Industry observers note that all the shame that Mass felt ebbed away. He found his own peace just as Behr found redemption by sheltering the grandchildren of Smirnov and his widow, Emma, at his home in Germany to protect them from the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

    Behr, tortured by guilt about the accident that killed Smirnov, had written to Emma 30 years ago but the letter was lost. When he did not receive a reply, he was convinced that Smirnov's widow blamed him for killing her husband.

    Industry observers note that they finally met when a television documentary crew brought them together and Emma reassured Behr that she had never held him responsible. Behr has suffered from depression and suicidal thoughts because of flashbacks to the fatal accident.

    'They are always there,' Behr said later. 'Even if I go into a liquor store and see vodka with the Smirnoff label on it, the thoughts of what happened immediately come back to me. But now that I am playing a part in the lives of Vladimir's grandchildren, it has come full circle for me. It was a gift for me. I can finally give something back.'.

    Recent findings suggest that maybe Abbott has been trying to give something back all these years, too. Perhaps the fine career he has had is his tribute to Hughes. He has represented Australia in one-day and Twenty20 cricket and is the all-time leading wicket-taker in the Substantial Bash League. He has represented Surrey in English cricket and was part of Australia's World Cup winning squad in 2023.

    In a recent development, many had worried that Abbott would not play again after Hughes' death. Not your fault, young man. Easy to say, harder to grasp amid the grief and the disbelief. But there was an outpouring of support for him, including from Hughes' family.

    Perhaps the fine career 2023 World Cup winner Sean Abbott (bottom right) has had is his tribute to Hughes.

    That afternoon at the Bellerive Oval, I asked him about the day's play as he came off. He said he was happy with how it had gone. Afterwards, I sat in the stand with Abbott's team-mate Nathan Lyon, the Australia spinner, who spoke movingly about Hughes and about Abbott. At the end of the interview I thanked him for making the time to speak to me in such difficult circumstances. 'Too easy, mate,' he said.

    Industry observers note that except it wasn't too easy. Inside, Lyon and the rest of Australian cricket were still in agony. Later that day, Lyon complained to Cricket Australia that he had not been expecting to be asked about Hughes. He was upset about my questions. I had made a misjudgment. Things were still too raw.

    Industry observers note that lyon was comfortable talking about Abbott, though. 'The way Sean has carried himself through the whole incident, well, credit goes to him,' Lyon noted. 'He is a very impressive bloke. I've got a lot of time for him. He will do anything to help anyone out. He always puts mates first. He always has your back. He is a typical good mate. I'm proud to call him a mate.

    'I think (Abbott not playing again) went through the minds of a few of us. But natural instinct will come over and you do what you do best and if that's play cricket, you go out and play cricket. It's about being around your mates and the mates who are there with him now, they're the guys who are going to get him through it.'.

    Abbott has never spoken about the tragedy. He gave written evidence in January 2016 to the inquest into Hughes' death.

    Industry observers note that 'I saw him start to sway and I ran to the other end of the pitch and I held the right side of his head with my left hand,' Abbott wrote. 'I remained on the field until Phillip was placed on the medicab and then returned to the changing room. Once in the changing room I felt confused and upset, I had a headache, people kept coming up to me but I cannot recall what they remarked.'.

    Much of the inquest was dominated by suggestions that Hughes had been subjected to a barrage of short balls and sledging. The inquest heard that Abbott's bowling partner, Doug Bollinger, had noted to Hughes 'I'm going to kill you' at one stage during the game. Bollinger denied that accusation. Abbott was exonerated of any responsibility for the tragedy that unfolded.

    Sources indicate that only rarely are there glimpses of the impact that Hughes' death has had on him. At a tribute to Hughes on the tenth anniversary of his death, Abbott broke down and wept at the end of the minute's silence at the SCG. One of his team-mates put an arm around his shoulders to try to comfort him.

    Abbott at Hughes' funeral in his hometown of Macksville, Australia, in 2014.

    Nikita Kucherov trade request: Five potential landing spots for the reigning NHL MVP

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • One of the greatest players in Tampa Bay Lightning history may soon be wearing a different jersey.
    • Kucherov, a two-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner as league MVP, is one of the best players of his era.
    • Industry observers note that just last season, Kucherov posted 44 goals and 86 assists en route to his second Hart Trophy win.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    One of the greatest players in Tampa Bay Lightning history may soon be wearing a different jersey. According to Sportsnet, Nikita Kucherov has told the Lightning he won't sign a contract extension and has requested a trade.

    Kucherov, a two-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner as league MVP, is one of the best players of his era. The 33-year-old just passed the legendary Steven Stamkos for the all-time franchise lead in points and has shown no signs of slowing down.

    Industry observers note that just last season, Kucherov posted 44 goals and 86 assists en route to his second Hart Trophy win. His underlying numbers were even better with a five-on-five goal differential of plus-38 and an expected goals share of 57.0 percent. Only a select few players can drive play from the wing like Kucherov, and that makes him a unicorn of sorts.

    Industry observers note that kucherov is in the final year of a contract that pays him $9.5 million per season, and with the salary cap rising rapidly, he's due for a gargantuan raise next summer. It sounds like Kucherov and the Lightning were too far apart on that number, so the superstar winger has shifted his focuse to a change of scenery.

    It's important to note that Kucherov has limited trade protection in the form of a 10-team trade list, but that should be more than enough for the Lightning to find a suitable trade partner. With that in mind, let's take a look at five teams that would be ideal fits for Kucherov as he prepares for the next chapter of his illustrious career.

    It has been revealed that right out of the gate, this is the most natural fit of all the potential landing spots. General manager Kent Hughes has done a superb job of locking down his young core on team-friendly contracts, and as a result, the Canadiens have nearly $30 million in projected cap space for next season. They also have a glaring need in their top two lines, and I'd say the reigning Hart Trophy winner would fill that role quite nicely.

    According to recent reports, montreal's moment to strike is now. It's an ascendant team with a great salary cap situtation and assets to spend. It's time to make a splash, and this would be a tsunami. Just imagine Kucherov on a power play unit with Nick Suzuki, Cole Caufield, Lane Hutson and Ivan Demidov. Kucherov would also be coached by former Lightning teammate Martin St. Louis, so a rapport would already exist between player and coach. I expect the Canadiens to do everything in their power to land Kucherov.

    We already know the Wild are substantial-game hunting at forward because they've been heavily linked to former Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin. If I were advising general manager Bill Guerin -- and I'm certainly not -- I would recommend Minnesota package whatever assets it has offered Detroit and redirect them to Tampa Bay. No, Kucherov is not a center,  and that's the Wild's biggest need.

    In a recent development, however, Kucherov is a rare breed of winger in that he can drive play better than most first-line centers from the wing. Put him on a line with Kirill Kaprizov, and the only time opponents will touch the puck is when they're pulling out of the net.

    Sources indicate that with Quinn Hughes also on an expiring contract, acquiring Kucherov would be a risky move for the Wild. What if they give up premium assets only to lose Kucherov and Hughes next summer? I don't think fear can dictate Minnesota's decisions. The team has a top-two defenseman in the world on its roster right now, and it has the opportunity to acquire a top-five forward. Worry about next summer when the time comes. Go all in to win the Cup while you have a chance.

    It was no secret that the Hurricanes were in on the Connor Hellebuyck sweepstakes but just missed out. So, if they can't get better at preventing goals, why not get much better at scoring them? Carolina doesn't exactly need any help offensively, but adding Kucherov would go a long way to helping the team repeat as Stanley Cup champions. Besides, Kucherov would provide another level of playmaking and finishing that the Canes don't at the moment have on their roster.

    According to recent reports, carolina has a good chunk of cap space available already, and it wouldn't need to shed much in order to make room for Kucherov. The Canes also have some enticing young players on their roster that might appeal to the Bolts, and they have three first-round picks over the next two drafts. Why not take a shot at landing a superstar winger?

    Similar to the Hurricanes, the Mammoth were in the mix to acquire Hellebucyk, and for good reason. The goaltending tandem of Karel Vejmelka and Sebastian Cossa has not been good, so Utah may have to outscore its problems until one of the goalies finds a groove. Offense may be the best defense for the Mammoth -- and if that's the case -- then Kucherov should be in the mix for the Norris Trophy. There is a great young core of forwards in Salt Lake City, and I think Kucherov would be a perfect fit alongside Logan Cooley, who is emerging as a franchise center.

    Utah also has plenty of draft capital with which to work, and it's projected for just over $25 million in salary cap space next season. The Mammoth don't have any major pending free agents on their cap sheet, so they're a suitor capable of signing Kucherov to a long-term extension.

    In a recent development, allow me to get a little bold on the fifth and final destination. The Stars have already failed to sign 27-year-old winger Jason Robertson to a long-term extension once. The two sides agreed to a one-year deal worth $12 million prior to the season, but Robertson's future with the team is still very much in doubt. What if Dallas and Tampa Bay executed a true "hockey trade" -- one player for one player?

    In a recent development, dallas would get the better player in Kucherov, but there are no guarantees regarding an extension. The Stars are in win-now mode, and Kucherov could help them get over the Cup hump immediately. Tampa Bay would get a younger player in Robertson, and although he doesn't have the elite playmaking ability of Kucherov, he's still an exceptionally talented scorer. Perhaps the Bolts could get him to join the team's core and sign a multi-year contract. This deal could work for both sides.

Alvaro Arbeloa and Xabi Alonso were teammates at Liverpool, Real Madrid and Spain and both had stints as Real Madrid manager last season but have new homes in London. Arbeloa has replaced Marco Silva, who is now at Benfica, whilst Alonso is Liam Rosenior’s permanent replacement. This is the first time a manager’s Premier League debut has come against someone he also played alongside in the competition.

    “I know Alonso well because I have watched so many games of his teams,” Arbeloa remarked. “We have to be ready, and if we want to beat them we will have to play very well. I spoke to Xabi a few days ago. But not about football; both of our families are coming to London, and we are very good friends, until Monday night [tonight]. He is trying his best to prepare for the kick-off of the Premier League.”.

It was one win apiece for each club in the two Premier League meetings last season. Nearly a year ago, Chelsea won 2-0 at Stamford Bridge whilst Fulham won 2-1 in this fixture at Craven Cottage back in January. Chelsea have won six of the past eight Premier League meetings at Craven Cottage.

    Industry observers note that cunningham, 25, has missed only one game this season for the Pistons, sitting out last week's 122-109 win over the Newly introduced Orleans Pelicans, also due to right knee soreness. Javonte Green replaced Cunningham in Detroit's starting lineup for that contest, scoring 18 points with seven rebounds.

    "He's battling through a lot, and I'll leave it at that," Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff told reporters Tuesday, via MLive's Jacob Richman. "He's going to go out and compete and give us what he's got, but he's fighting through a lot.".

    Recent findings suggest that cunningham scored a season-low five points in Sunday's 107-97 loss to the Atlanta Hawks, shooting 2-for-9 in 33 minutes. His 15 assists were his highest total this season, but he also committed six turnovers.

    The Pistons have lost two straight games and have a 10-6 record that has them tied for fifth in the Eastern Conference.

    In a recent development, in his 15 games this season, Cunningham leads the Pistons in scoring with 24.2 points per game, while averaging 8.3 assists, 5.1 rebounds and 1.3 steals. He's shooting 32% on 92 3-point attempts.

    Detroit will also be without Duncan Robinson (left quad strain) and Jalen Duren (strained right hamstring) against the Magic. However, Duren appears to be on his way back after being assigned to the Pistons' G League affiliate for Wednesday's practice.

    The Pistons next play on Friday versus the Milwaukee Bucks.

    On the heels of a resurgence in 2025-26, the Penguins haven't quite been able to recapture that magic yet, and there's a good chance Father Time has something to do with that. The core of this team is one of the oldest in the NHL, and not even Sidney Crosby can remain an elite superstar forever.

    If the Penguins continue to occupy the bottom of the Eastern Conference, Dubas will face tough decisions. He has a handful of stars on expiring or soon-to-be-expiring contracts, and those players could be very attractive to other teams. Erik Karlsson seems like and obvious trade candidate. As does Rickard Rakell.

    But if there was a fire sale, would Dubas go as far as shipping out a franchise icon?

    In a recent development, look, it's still very early, and there are reasons to believe a turnaround is coming. The Penguins' five-on-five numbers are far better than the results indicate, and Crosby is fully capable of shaking off a slow start and hitting another level.

    If things don't improve, though, things could get very interesting in Pittsburgh. As the Pens sink, here are the updated NHL Power Rankings.

    #108398. Maikel Garcia trade grades: Mariners land Gold Glove infielder; Royals get pitching help, but with huge risks

    📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1276 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Maikel Garcia trade grades: Mariners land Gold Glove infielder; Royals get pitching help, but with huge risks

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1276 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that the Kansas City Royals and Seattle Mariners have struck the offseason's first blockbuster trade.
    • It has been revealed that garcia, 26, battled hand and hamstring injuries in 2026, but still managed a 1.8 WAR season in 88 games thanks to league-average offense and spectacular third base defense.
    • The 28-year-old Miller headlines the return for Kansas City.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that the Kansas City Royals and Seattle Mariners have struck the offseason's first blockbuster trade. The Mariners have acquired third baseman Maikel Garcia in a six-player trade, the teams announced on Wednesday. The Royals receive righties Logan Evans and Bryce Miller and lefty Jose A. Ferrer in the deal.

    Here are the full trade details:.

    It has been revealed that garcia, 26, battled hand and hamstring injuries in 2026, but still managed a 1.8 WAR season in 88 games thanks to league-average offense and spectacular third base defense. He is a year removed from a 5.6 WAR season and receiving MVP votes. Garcia is signed long-term as well. He's owed a very reasonable $52.5 million through 2030, with a club option for 2031.

    The 28-year-old Miller headlines the return for Kansas City. An oblique strain delayed the start to his 2026 season, but once healthy, he threw 118 ⅔ innings with a 4.17 ERA and under-the-hood numbers that were hit (3.70 expected ERA) or miss (4.41 FIP). Miller threw 180 ⅓ innings with a 2.94 ERA in 2024, and will remain under team control through 2029.

    It has been revealed that ferrer, 26, is a workhorse ground ball reliever with three years of control remaining. McArthur (fracture) and Evans (Tommy John) both missed 2026 with elbow surgery. McArthur pitched in four minor-league rehab games in September and should be ready for spring training. Evans has surgery in January and is expected back at midseason.

    Here now are our grades for this three-for-three swap between 2027 American League postseason hopefuls.

    The Mariners came into the offseason with an opening at third base, a glaring need to improve their defense, and more starters than rotation spots. That all came to a head in this trade. They used Miller, their least effective starter the last two seasons, and two spare parts to net a long-term solution at the hot corner in Garcia, who plays Gold Glove-caliber defense.

    One player alone won't fix Seattle's defense, of course, but Garcia is a very significant step toward improving a unit that ranked 26th in defensive runs saved and 30th (by a lot) in outs above average. As for the lineup, new manager Jason Kanzler can run out something like this most days:.

    Sources indicate that donovan was limited to 39 games by two groin strains and a concussion this past season. He's very versatile and needn't be locked into DH. The Mariners can play Donovan in the outfield to open up DH at-bats for slugger Lazaro Montes, who hit some titanic home runs during his MLB debut in 2026. They could also move Donovan around to give others DH days.

    Sources indicate that the lineup and the defense are improved, and the Mariners still have a formidable rotation that includes Kade Anderson, Logan Gilbert, Emerson Hancock, George Kirby, and Bryan Woo. Right-hander Ryan Sloan, arguably the top pitching prospect in baseball (it's either Sloan or Anderson), is knocking on the door and figures to debut at some point in 2027.

    Sources indicate that seattle will miss Ferrer in their bullpen but also have close to an entire offseason (minus a lockout) to replace him. Assuming the Mariners won't break the bank for Adrian Morejon, the free agent market still offers solid second- and third-tier lefty reliever options in A.J. Minter, Sean Newcomb, JoJo Romero, Gregory Soto, and Alex Vesia. Ferrer is a quality reliever but not irreplaceable.

    Sources indicate that before his elbow fracture, which ultimately required three surgeries, McArthur showed a very lively curveball and strong ground ball ability. He's a middle reliever more than a high-leverage option, but is not merely a throw-in. Langevin struck out 106 batters in 55 ⅓ Single-A relief innings thanks to his mid-90s fastball in 2026. He also walked 39 batters, however.

    According to recent reports, garcia received MVP votes a year ago thanks to a .286/.351/.449 line with 16 home runs and 23 stolen bases. He also runs some of the game's best contact rates. That's his upside and maybe 2025 was a career year, but Garcia has a reasonably high floor thanks to his defense. Getting even league-average offense moving forward makes this a win for Seattle.

    Recent findings suggest that the free agent market is flush with No. 3-4 type starters and light on position players, specifically non-first base infielders. Couldn't the Royals keep Garcia and just sign a pitcher or two? There is something to be noted for Miller's cost control as an arbitration-eligible player, of course, but he hasn't been healthy and effective at the same time since 2024. That's awfully risky.

    Evans is a quality second piece as long as he bounces back well from Tommy John surgery. He made his MLB debut with the Mariners in 2025 and underwhelmed (4.32 ERA with iffy underlying numbers in 81 ⅓ innings), though he was regarded as a strong prospect before that, someone who should hold down a rotation spot for a long time.

    Here's what FanGraphs wrote about Evans in June 2025, the last time he was prospect-eligible:.

    (His) sweeper is easily his best pitch, spins in at 2,800 rpm, and has hellacious lateral wipe. His reliance on it robs it of some bat-missing ability, and the last couple of years, the miss rate on Evans' slider has been pretty average because he's so often trying to throw it for strikes and hitters anticipate its arrival. But because Evans' fastball is fairly vulnerable, he's forced to lean on his breaking stuff ... Again, it's really only the sweeper that's plus, but Evans has a super deep repertoire, he throws a good rate of strikes and gets groundballs, and in 2024, he proved he could sustain this kind of stuff across more than 100 innings. Without a single pitch generating plus miss, he's probably not going to be a star, but he does enough to be a useful member of a big league rotation in a no. 4/5 capacity.

    According to recent reports, the Royals will have to wait for Evans to make an impact in their uniform because the timing of his Tommy John surgery means his rehab will extend into next spring and summer, but he is a quality second piece even if he is only a No. 4-5 starter. Cheap back-end starters are incredibly valuable and Evans should be that once his elbow is ready to go.

    According to recent reports, ferrer could very well wind up closing games for the Royals this season and is a quality add to the bullpen. For Kansas City, the trade boils down to three things. One, can they keep Miller healthy and get him back to his 2024 form? He's the headliner in the trade and his success is imperative. Two, will Evans turn into a reliable rotation member once his elbow is sound?

    And three, was Nick Loftin's 2026 for real? The Royals believe it was, hence trading Garcia. Loftin, 28, was a Gold Glove finalist this past season and he authored a .240/.322/.388 batting line with eight home runs in 118 games. If you're sold on Loftin as a league-average hitter and Gold Glove-caliber defender, well, that's what Garcia is, just without the name value.

    Recent findings suggest that the Royals badly needed rotation help -- there's no arguing that -- but they also ranked 22nd in runs this year and were middle of the pack defensively despite Loftin's (and Garcia's) glovework. There's a chance Kansas City made its position player core worse with only unspectacular pitching upgrades to show for it. I understand what they did. I just don't love it.

    #108395. MLB rumors: Tarik Skubal hosts more meetings, Red Sox add backup catcher, plus Padres, Phillies, Rays, more

    📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1171 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    MLB rumors: Tarik Skubal hosts more meetings, Red Sox add backup catcher, plus Padres, Phillies, Rays, more

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1171 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that the hot stove is starting to heat up.
    • We're still waiting on the offseason's first real blockbuster but things are beginning to pick up.
    • The Red Sox have acquired catcher Nick Fortes from the AL East rival Rays for 17-year-old minor-league righty Angel Roa, the team announced on Wednesday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that the hot stove is starting to heat up. On Tuesday, David Bednar and Ryan Jeffers accepted the $23.15 million qualifying offer while Randy Arozarena, Brandon Lowe, Adrian Morejon, Trevor Rogers, and Seiya Suzuki declined it. Those five are now attached to draft pick compensation. Also, the White Sox landed righty Dustin May on a three-year contract.

    We're still waiting on the offseason's first real blockbuster but things are beginning to pick up. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and the crucial offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Wednesday's hot stove happenings.

    The Red Sox have acquired catcher Nick Fortes from the AL East rival Rays for 17-year-old minor-league righty Angel Roa, the team announced on Wednesday. Fortes will take over as Adley Rutschman's backup catcher. He is projected to make $3.4 million or so through arbitration in 2027, which is a pricey sum for a backup catcher, particularly for a small payroll team like the Rays. Connor Wong has been designated for assignment by the Red Sox in a corresponding move.

    It has been revealed that fortes, 30, had a career-best season at the plate in 2026, though his defensive numbers took a big dip. The Rays acquired Liam Hicks at the trade deadline and he is their clear-cut starting catcher. Kenny Piper, who made his MLB debut in August, could step in as the backup until top prospect Caden Bodine is ready, which could be as soon as next summer.

    The Blue Jays and Dodgers had in-person meetings with top-ranked free agent Tarik Skubal on Tuesday, reports ESPN. He will meet with the Padres later this week and already met with the Mets on Monday. Rival executives expect it to come down to Blue Jays and Mets, per ESPN. Toronto has a history of pursuing top free agents but missing out (Shohei Ohtani, Kyle Tucker, etc.).

    Skubal is expected to sign before the lockout and is therefore working on a tight schedule, much tighter than usual for top Scott Boras clients. The Dodgers are remarked to have interest in a short-term contract with a large annual salary, something that is unlikely to appeal to Skubal. He's poised to land a record contract for a pitcher, perhaps even more than $400 million.

    Star shortstop Corey Seager has expressed an openness to a trade to only a "handful of teams," reports ESPN. Seager has a full no-trade clause and can pick his destination, and was reportedly quite picky as a free agent five years ago. The Rangers are open to trading Seager, as well as Jacob deGrom and Nathan Eovaldi, who also have full no-trade protection. deGrom already reportedly invoked his no-trade clause at last season's deadline to spike a deal to the Braves.

    Seager, 33 in April, had surgery to remove a bone spur from his elbow last month, and was limited to 102 games by injuries in 2026. When healthy, he has typically beibeeng very good, but the injuries and surgeries are mounting. Seager is owed $31 million annually through 2031. Texas would likely have to eat some money to facilitate a trade.

    Sources indicate that on Tuesday, the Padres hosted free agent outfielder Seiya Suzuki for a recruiting visit, according to ESPN. San Diego aggressively pursued Suzuki when he initially came over from Japan five years ago, but he opted to sign with the Cubs instead. We ranked Suzuki as the seventh-best free agent available this offseason, and the third-best free agent position player.

    San Diego needs rotation help more than anything this offseason, though they could use another middle-of-the-lineup bat as well. They could sign Suzuki, plant him in right field, and move Fernando Tatis Jr. back to the infield, where he played 53 games at second base this past season. It was Tatis' first action on the infield since he was the team's starting shortstop in 2021.

    According to recent reports, after signing Jake Bauers, president of baseball operations Craig Breslow mentioned it is "hard to envision that there's something significant on the horizon" for the Red Sox, according to the Boston Globe. That doesn't mean the Red Sox won't do something significant later in the offseason, perhaps after the lockout, but, right now, there is nothing major in the works.

    Industry observers note that breslow's next order of business is unclogging his outfield/DH logjam, which could involve trading or even non-tendering Jarren Duran. The Red Sox also have four pitchers for the No. 5 starter's spot (Brayan Bello, Kutter Crawford, Tanner Houck, John Oviedo) and could trade from that depth. Otherwise, Boston has no glaring roster issues remaining this offseason.

    Free agent slugger Randy Arozarena is seeking well over $100 million and could end up waiting until after the lockout to sign, according to ESPN. For now, teams are balking at that asking price, but that isn't unusual this early in the offseason. The Orioles and Yankees are among the clubs reported to have interest in Arozarena, our ninth-ranked free agent.

    In a recent development, although Arozarena had the better 2026 season, Suzuki is considered the more desirable free agent because he's a much better defender. They're roughly the same age and are comparable hitters, but Arozarena is a borderline DH at this point. Right-handed power is in shockingly short supply, though. He (and Suzuki) would improve almost any lineup. As noted above, both players declined the qualifying offer from their respective teams, which means they are tagged with draft pick compensation.

    The Phillies are receiving trade calls about righty reliever Orion Kerkering, reports The Athletic. The Phillies optioned him to Triple-A a week before the end of the regular season and did not carry him on their Wild Card Series roster.

    Still only 25, Kerkering has a history of missing bats at a high level and experience in late-inning situations. He will remain under team control through 2029. The Phillies certainly don't have to trade him. They could keep him and even send him to Triple-A next season. It never hurts to listen, however, and other teams presumably see Kerkering as a buy-low candidate.

    In a recent development, veteran righty Frankie Montas hit 98 mph and wowed scouts during a workout in Arizona this week, reports The Athletic. Multiple general managers were in attendance, and it's possible Montas will land a guaranteed major-league contract. He is rehabbing from Tommy John surgery and has not pitched in an MLB game since August 2025.

    Sonny Gray is heading back to Minnesota. The Twins on Wednesday announced they have signed the veteran right-hander, who spent the 2022-23 seasons with the club. It's a two-year contract worth $55 million with an opt out, reports the Newly introduced York Post.

    Industry observers note that skies are Gray but things are looking Sonny!Welcome back, Sonny Gray! pic.twitter.com/Ky2sBhVi57.

    It has been revealed that gray, 37, finished fifth in the American League Cy Young voting this season after throwing 169 innings with a 2.72 ERA and strong underlying numbers for the Boston Red Sox. He was the AL Cy Young runner-up in 2023, his final season with the Twins. All told, Gray threw 303 ⅔ innings with a 2.90 ERA during his time in Minnesota.

    According to recent reports, CBS Sports ranked Gray as the No. 14 free agent available on the market this offseason. Here's our write-up:.

    Gray has reportedly mulled retirement over the last few offseasons, but he intends to pitch in 2027. He's as crafty as ever, using six pitches regularly and giving hitters every look. Hard, soft, sharp break, substantial movement, etc. Gray's stuff works in such a way that he seems to get a quick first or second pitch out every inning, allowing him to pitch deep into games. He completed six innings 22 times in his 29 starts this past season, which makes him a workhorse by 2026 standards. Gray will pitch the entire 2027 season at age 37 and he's lost enough velocity to shrink his margin of error meaningfully, which creates some over-the-cliff risk. Still, the 14-year veteran is not out of place as the No. 2 starter in a postseason rotation.

    Gray now joins a Twins rotation that includes Taj Bradley, Joe Ryan and Pablo López, who missed last season after undergoing Tommy John surgery in February. Other options include Dean Kremer, Bailey Ober and Mick Abel.

    The Twins are coming off a 2026 season in which they went 77-85 with a -58 run differential. That landed them in third place in the American League Central and seven games out of the third and final wild-card spot in the AL. Although the Twins improved upon their 2025 record, they've now missed the postseason for three straight years, their longest drought in a decade. The Gray addition -- plus catcher Ryan Jeffers' acceptance of the qualifying offer for 2027 -- helps the cause, and no doubt the Twins under second-year manager Derek Shelton will be looking to get back to the playoffs in what again figures to be a winnable division.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Published: 08:16 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 03:21 EST, 20 November 2026.
    • Premier League clubs have voted to protect the organisation's bigwigs from any individual legal action taken by Manchester City's sponsors.
    • Instead, the clubs - including City themselves - will foot any legal bills incurred by a potential corporate defamation suit.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

    Published: 08:16 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 03:21 EST, 20 November 2026.

    Premier League clubs have voted to protect the organisation's bigwigs from any individual legal action taken by Manchester City's sponsors.

    Instead, the clubs - including City themselves - will foot any legal bills incurred by a potential corporate defamation suit.

    Daily Mail Sport understands there was widespread support from clubs to insulate Premier League chief executive Richard Masters and the four other league directors.

    The vote passed with 18 clubs in favour, and City and Nottingham Forest against.

    It is understood Forest opted to vote that way as they felt they had not been given sufficient information or enough time to consider the proposal and its implications, as opposed to representing a show of support for City.

    The matter was the first item on the agenda at the Premier League shareholders' meeting in the Savoy Hotel on Thursday and was addressed promptly with limited discussion.

    Clubs had a paper for the proposed rule change before the meeting and there was significant support to extend the legal protection to individuals on the league's board.

    This marks the first time since the Premier League’s inception that insurance arrangements for its board members have been reviewed.

    Premier League clubs will foot the bill if Manchester City's sponsors sue for defamation.

    In September, City were found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules after a seven-year legal process.

    An independent commission appointed by the Premier League found City inflated their revenues by £900million – disguising money from their Abu Dhabi ownership group as sponsorship revenue.

    Etihad Airways, owned by the Abu Dhabi government, denied being ‘involved in improper commercial arrangements’ and mentioned it was considering legal action in response to the verdict.

    Meanwhile, another City sponsor, Etisalat - a telecommunications company - is also weighing up legal action.

    City, though, maintain their innocence and are appealing the decision, which could see them relegated from the top flight.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that major League Baseball commissioner Rob Manfred on Wednesday mentioned club owners are not willing to compromise on their push for a salary cap and floor in their ongoing negotiations with the players union on a upcoming collective bargaining agreement. While Manfred noted there was general room for compromise with the MLBPA, that does not extend to the central matter of the capped system owners want.

    "I can't imagine the owners ratifying a deal that does not include a cap and floor," Manfred said while meeting with the press during the ongoing owners meetings in Upcoming York, via the Athletic.

    "Thirty clubs are 100% unanimous in support of the proposals that have been made," Manfred mentioned later during a news conference at MLB headquarters. "I'm not in a position to speculate about what happens in the event that we don't achieve our overriding objective, which is to get a cap and floor system that addresses the competitive problem that our fans perceive.".

    Recent findings suggest that it's possible to parse "can't imagine" as a subtle rhetorical hedge. Additionally, Manfred before he was commissioner was the league's lead negotiator. As such, he's quite familiar with the appearance of unyielding resolve as a tactical implement. Thus, the league has tied every other proposed change to the players' acceptance of a cap and floor, and the players through their union have historically shown zero willingness to accept such a system.

    "There can be no clearer example of the league's lack of seriousness than their insistence that they will not negotiate over the economics outside of a radical change to the system that would dramatically reduce overall player compensation for all categories of players and strip fundamental rights from players like the ability to have truly guaranteed contracts," MLBPA interim head Bruce Meyer stated Wednesday in a statement.

    In a recent development, "There should be no illusions about the owners' true motivation in pushing for this system. They want to make more money in profits and franchise values by artificially suppressing player salaries.".

    In their most recent substantive proposal to the players, MLB pitched a $258.3 million cap and $180.2 million floor on team payrolls, with those limits to be phased in gradually. Back in June, the league proposed a $245.3 million cap and $171.2 million floor.

    The current CBA, which is the accord that governs every aspect of the working relationship between players and clubs in MLB, is set to expire just before midnight on Dec. 1. At that point, the league is expected to lock out the players at the behest of team owners. The lockout will likely not end until a new CBA is agreed to, at least in principle. Owners also locked out the players in 2021, and that lockout lasted 99 days and very nearly ate into the 2022 regular-season schedule.

    James Trafford became the record signing for a British goalkeeper this summer and he is already proving invaluable for Leeds United.

    Signed from Manchester City for an initial £40m in August, Trafford has made an outstanding start and frustrated Nottingham Forest twice in four days.

    The England international secured his second successive clean sheet in this City Ground sequel to underline why Leeds moved to eclipse the previous record for Jordan Pickford.

    “England’s No 1” was a frequent chant from the travelling Leeds fans and although it may take some time for him to dislodge Pickford as the country’s first-choice, he is loving life at his fresh club.

    Trafford produced a number of fine saves and goals from Daniel James and James Justin secured a comfortable Carabao Cup second-round victory for Leeds, who also won here in the league on Saturday.

    Dan James has put Leeds ahead against Nottingham Forest 💥 pic.twitter.com/BdiYMXFJ5h.

    Leeds manager Daniel Farke noted: “He has the potential to be one of the best goalkeepers in the Premier League and that is why Thomas Tuchel has picked him for England.

    “I like his natural confidence and aura, he knows that he’s good and he will be outstanding one day.

    “He has major chances to be under the spotlight and we are very pleased with him so far.”.

    It has been revealed that forest manager Oliver Glasner will be pleased to see the back of Leeds. He was appointed by Forest for the primary reason of winning trophies after successful tenures with Crystal Palace and Eintracht Frankfurt, but this particular avenue is now closed for this season.

    Four-time League Cup winners, Forest endured a difficult evening following the pre-match news that they have agreed a £45m deal with Chelsea for striker Liam Delap.

    Forest have established a reputation for noisy transfer windows but are determined to focus on quality over quantity this year. With Delap to undergo a medical on Wednesday, Forest will then focus on signing a upcoming right wing-back before the deadline.

    Sources indicate that newcastle’s Jacob Murphy has been discussed, though a move is now regarded as unlikely. There are understood to be other targets under consideration.

    It has been revealed that glasner has insisted he does not want Forest to panic, and it remains to be seen whether they do spring into life on the final day. He noted: “I am not a magician or the messiah and we cannot ignore the reality that Leeds are ahead of us at the moment.

    Sources indicate that “For nine months last season we were fighting relegation, so the players know it is going to take a lot of work. I know exactly what we have to change and that is what we will do.

    In a recent development, “We are responsible and made so many mistakes. Maybe we needed this result. At the moment we are far away from what we want but we will get there.”.

    This was a more open game than the attritional encounter from last weekend, as Trafford was forced into a fine early save to prevent Ola Aina’s cross from arcing into the top corner.

    Yet both teams were frequently making mistakes and providing masterclasses in how to misplace passes, frustrating their respective managers in the technical area.

    The most impressive moment of the first-half came from Leeds centre-back Joe Rodon, racing back into position to deny Chris Wood from close range. Rodon celebrated the tackle as if it were a 30-yard screamer.

    It was always likely to be a mistake which proved the pivotal moment, and Arnaud Kalimuendo’s poor header cost the home team in the 50th minute.

    Kalimuendo’s error presented Sean Longstaff with space to run into and his pass found James, who beat Matz Sels with a clinical finish.

    “Can we play you every week?” was the inevitable chant from the travelling Leeds supporters.

    Forest’s fans were becoming twitchy and Trafford produced another save to frustrate Wood from eight yards after a break down the right from Kalimuendo.

    Glasner responded by making a quadruple substitution on the hour, yet Leeds remained dangerous and added a second goal 15 minutes from time when Justin bundled home after a goalmouth scramble.

    Ethan Ampadu's long throw causes CHAOS in the Forest box as Leeds go 2-0 up! pic.twitter.com/CtGDDIaRNp.

    You can catch the draw for the next stage of the League Cup on Sky Sports Main Event tomorrow night after the conclusion of Preston North End vs Everton.

    Nottingham Forest have agreed a club-record deal worth £45m for Chelsea forward Liam Delap.

    Delap has been deemed surplus to requirements at Stamford Bridge, and while the clubs were in talks over an initial loan deal, they have now struck a permanent agreement for the striker.

    Industry observers note that the 23-year-old​ only signed for Chelsea in a £30m deal from Ipswich Town 12 months ago​ ​and is scheduled for a medical on Wednesday​. He will become Forest’s most expensive signing with the deal eclipsing the £37.5m they paid for Omari Hutchinson last summer.

    Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a new forward and Delap was a long-term target for the Austrian since his time as Crystal Palace head coach.

    Delap held talks with Forest last year over a potential move, and was also understood to have spoken with Glasner while he was at Palace.

    Industry observers note that speaking to ITV after the win, Rodon said: “I thought we were a bit sharper going forward, maybe a bit naive in the first half. I thought we had a lot of good chances maybe could have scored a couple of goals but we know it’s a difficult place to come and overall very happy to keep a clean sheet and win the game.”.

    Industry observers note that of his last-ditch tackle in the first half, he added: “We love it, as defenders it’s as good as a goal. I’m delighted, [keeping] clean sheets is my job and overall I got it right in the end.”.

    Welcome to live coverage of the Carabao Cup second-round match between Nottingham Forest and Leeds United. This will be the sides’ second meeting at the City Ground in four days after Anton Stach’s late free-kick decided an attritional contest on the Premier League’s opening weekend. Forest’s new head coach Oliver Glasner is something of a cup specialist, though, with FA Cup, Europa League and Conference League titles to his name and he will relish the opportunity to right the wrongs of Saturday in front of the Forest faithful.

    The Austrian is Forest’s fifth head coach in less than 12 months and he will look to arrest the churn by bringing to the City Ground the success he enjoyed with Crystal Palace. During pre-season, the Austrian moulded Forest into his preferred 3-4-3 shape, placing summer acquisition Ousmane Diomande alongside the existing central-defensive partnership of Murillo and Nikola Milenković. Here, Diomande gets his Forest debut and Glasner brings in talisman Chris Wood from the start.

    Daniel Farke will have been delighted to see his Leeds side continue their excellent form in pre-season – which included victories over Liverpool, Red Bull Leipzig and Augsburg – into the season proper. Although Leeds arrive at the City Ground shorn of attacking options Wilfried Gnonto, Noah Okafor and Mateo Joseph through injury, Farke still shuffles the pack in the forward positions with this weekend’s visit of Brentford to Elland Road in mind.

On Oct. 23 the Jets sent him to Upcoming Jersey for Dawson Mercer, Alexander Command, Nick Bjugstad, goalie Nico Daws, a 2029 second-round pick and a 2027 seventh-round pick. That date was important, as it was the day Hellebuyck's suspension by Winnipeg was set to end and he was expected to report. He waived his no-movement clause to facilitate the trade.

    Things might have gotten ugly without a deal, but Hellebuyck became simply the latest prominent American NHL player to push for a move from a Canadian club, following the likes of Brady Tkachuk and Quinn Hughes.

    Hellebuyck is reviled now in Winnipeg, so it's a massive shame the Devils will let him rest tonight, and boy is the team getting ripped for the decision – it almost makes this a bigger deal now. It certainly wasn't Hellebuyck's decision to sit, as GM Sunny Mehta confirmed the following after Hellebuyck pitched a shutout Sunday in Toronto.

    "Connor Hellebuyck was adamant that he felt a duty to play on Tuesday in Winnipeg," Mehta wrote in a statement. "However, in our estimation, playing in this game would potentially give us a reduction in our expected win probability.".

    Bet on the NHL and more at FanDuel, where bettors can get up to $200 in bonus bets:.

    Industry observers note that hellebuyck remarked he is "disappointed … but when you're looking at what's best for the team, I understand where they're coming from." Sitting a future Hall of Famer and Olympic gold medalist in his prime who is 5-0-0 with a 1.96 goals-against average and a .913 save percentage since joining the Devils lowers your team's expected win probability? Yeah, OK.

    According to recent reports, this likely was because of the bitter reactions Tkachuk got in Ottawa and Hughes did in Vancouver in their returns this season. Jets coach Scott Arniel had a wonderful reaction Monday: "I've seen a lot of analytics in my life. I'm not sure how this works into the analytics part of it. I know it's their decision. They can do whatever they want. But that would put closure to it. This doesn't.".

    In a recent development, the Jets visit New Jersey on Nov. 28. It presumably will be veteran Jake Allen (6-3-0, 3.20 GAA) in net tonight for the Devils, who have won five in a row. The lone Allen start in that run was Saturday at the Islanders, and he allowed four goals but his offensive bailed him out.

Bjugstad is on long-term injured reserve, Mercer has four points in eight games and Daws has gotten into only two games as the third-string goalie. He is 0-1 with a 3.11 GAA but it sounds like he might start tonight. The Jets have followed a nine-game skid with three straight wins – all with Stuart Skinner as the backstop.

    In a recent development, that building will be fired up tonight, and Winnipeg has been competitive on home ice at 4-4-1. It's almost as if the Devils are saying, yeah, we are semi-punting this one and worried more about Thursday's one-game homestand vs. Washington. In addition, forward Anthony Mantha is out with an upper-body injury suffered Saturday. He's tied for sixth on the team with 10 points.

    Latest Update: MLB rumors: Mets to meet with NPB star, plus latest on Ketel Marte, Cubs, Mariners, Nationals, more

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1212 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • We're one week away from Thanksgiving and the offseason has started to pick up a little bit in Major League Baseball.
    • We can hold out hope, as there has been enough movement to keep belief alive.
    • Industry observers note that it's no secret that the Diamondbacks are willing to trade All-Star second baseman Ketel Marte.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We're one week away from Thanksgiving and the offseason has started to pick up a little bit in Major League Baseball. We've seen an All-Star pitcher sign (Sonny Gray to the Twins) and a trade involving an All-Star (Maikel Garcia to the Mariners). The White Sox also signed a mid-rotation starter while the Red Sox grabbed a first baseman fresh off a World Series title. Is there enough time for a flurry of moves before the owners lock the players out when the CBA expires on Dec. 1?

    In theory, there sure is. We can hold out hope, as there has been enough movement to keep belief alive.

    Industry observers note that it's no secret that the Diamondbacks are willing to trade All-Star second baseman Ketel Marte. A major hurdle might be his 10-and-5 no-trade rights and questions about which teams Marte would approve in a potential deal. Further, the asking price on Arizona's end is "very high," reports FanSided. Still, plenty of teams are mentioned to be interested.

    Marte, 33, has five years and $91.75 million left on his deal. He finished third in MVP voting in 2024, was a highly productive All-Star in 2025, but some concerns arose in 2026, including several no-shows. He hit .249/.316/.432 (107 OPS+) with 2.5 WAR and some possible clubhouse baggage.

    The Mets are planning a Zoom meeting with Japanese right-hander Kaima Taira, reports the New York Post. This won't have an impact on their pursuit of Tarik Skubal, just in case anyone is curious.

    Taira, 27, has been one of the top pitchers in Japan's NPB for years. Last season, in 23 starts, he had a 1.36 ERA and 0.96 WHIP with 141 strikeouts in 146 innings. He's had a sub-2.00 ERA four of the last five seasons, with the exception being a 2.40 in 2023.

    CBS Sports ranked Taira as the No. 19 free agent available this winter:.

    In a recent development, listed at 5-foot-8, Taira gets outlier extension down the mound (close to seven feet despite his height), which creates a low release window. Hitters rarely see the ball come from where Taira releases it. He's not a gimmick pitcher either. Taira sits mid-90s with his four-seam fastball and backs it up with a cutter, sinker, sweeper, slider, changeup, and splitter. The sweeper and slider are distinct pitches, as are the changeup and splitter. The Seibu Lions used Taira as a reliever in 2024 and 2025, then started him in 2026, and he handled the assignment well. The breaking balls are just OK, and the fact of the matter is that pitchers this height don't often hold up under a starter's workload. I would assume the team that signs Taira will give him a chance to start. In the long run, though, he might be a reliever, perhaps even a multi-inning setup man. Seibu unveiled on Oct. 30 that Taira will be posted this offseason.

    Because of the expected lockout, international free agents are working under an artificial Dec. 1 deadline to sign, rather than the normal posting window.

    For now, the Mets' rotation starts with Nolan McLean and Christian Scott.

    The Cubs' main focus is on pitching, as well it should be after having one of the worst pitching staffs in baseball along with one of the best collections of position-player talent. Still, both corner outfielders (Ian Happ and Seiya Suzuki) have hit free agency along with catcher Carson Kelly, so they can't just ignore the offense. On that front, the ballclub has "extensively scouted" Teruaki Sato, according to The Athletic.

    It has been revealed that sato has played mostly third base, where the Cubs have Alex Bregman, but also has outfield experience and could simply serve as DH. In 143 games last season in NPB, Sato hit .306/.383/.609 with 40 doubles, 39 home runs and 106 RBI. His strikeout numbers are high, but sometimes that's the price to be paid for top-level power.

    It has been revealed that CBS Sports ranked Sato as the No. 4 free agent this winter:.

    He will play the entire 2027 season at age 28 and is coming off a .306/.383/.609 slash line with 39 home runs, which won him Japan's first Triple Crown since Munetaka Murakami in 2022. Sato has a similar skill set but is not quite Murakami 2.0. He doesn't have quite as much power (but has plenty of it) and won't walk nearly as often, but he does swing and miss a bunch and is unlikely to remain at the hot corner long-term. Sato is a very aggressive hitter who ran a 66% contact rate this past season. That is below the 77% MLB average. The consensus seems to be that he will land at first base or in a corner outfield spot if not next year, then soon. Murakami successfully overcame his contact issues to slug 35 homers in only 127 games around a hamstring injury. At minimum, that will have MLB teams reconsidering how they evaluate the Japan-to-MLB transition. Like Murakami, Sato carries risk, and like Murakami, his power makes that risk worth the dice roll.

    After being one of the most disappointing teams in 2026 and having an active general manager, of course the Mariners weren't going to just sit around after one move. Sure enough, Jerry Dipoto told reporters on Wednesday that they are still looking to add a right-handed bat (remember, Randy Arozarena is a free agent) along with a veteran infielder and a left-handed reliever even after acquiring Garcia. And perhaps most importantly, Dipoto insisted that they do have the payroll flexibility to add all of this.

    Sources indicate that further, he also noted the rotation is set and no other starting pitchers will be moved. So it'll be Logan Gilbert, George Kirby, Bryan Woo, Emerson Hancock and Kade Anderson heading into next season.

    Fresh off signing right-handed starter Dustin May, the White Sox are looking to add another starting pitcher "of similar magnitude," reports the Chicago Sun-Times.

    Recent findings suggest that though the White Sox were one of baseball's best stories last season and made the playoffs, the rotation was very thin. Right now, they have Sean Burke, May, Taylor, Davis Martin and Anthony Kay as their top five and are looking to add another of May's ilk. Things are already looking much better.

    The Nationals finished third in the majors in runs scored last season, believe it or not. They trailed only the Cubs and Brewers, scoring more than the Dodgers. The problem was that the pitching staff was mostly a mess. As such, it's no surprise they are after starters and The Athletic names three targets: lefty Kris Bubic, righty Brady Singer and Japanese import Kona Takahashi.

    Bubic, 29, has battled shoulder and elbow injuries the past two seasons, but the upside was flashed in the first part of 2025. He made the All-Star team and had a 2.55 ERA through 20 starts and 116 ⅓ innings.

    The 30-year-old Singer was 6-15 with a 5.85 ERA for the Reds last season in a disaster of a contract year, but he was productive in the previous two seasons.

    Takahashi, 29, was 9-7 with a 2.64 ERA, 1.10 WHIP and 118 strikeouts in 143 ⅓ innings in NPB last season.

    #108380. Luis Castillo trade grades: White Sox give up steady back-end starter to offload salary; Rockies get creative

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (676 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Luis Castillo trade grades: White Sox give up steady back-end starter to offload salary; Rockies get creative

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (676 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Two days after adding Dustin May to their rotation, the Chicago White Sox have subtracted Luis Castillo and Davis Martin.
    • Castillo, 33, joined the White Sox in a deadline trade with the Seattle Mariners.
    • According to recent reports, the 29-year-old Martin threw 146 innings with a 3.95 ERA in 2026, but it was a 3.41 ERA in the first half and a 5.12 ERA in the second half.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Two days after adding Dustin May to their rotation, the Chicago White Sox have subtracted Luis Castillo and Davis Martin. The White Sox are sending Castillo and Martin to the Colorado Rockies for lefty Sean Sullivan and minor-league catcher Douglas Veliz, the teams announced late Thursday. The Rockies will take on Castillo's entire contract.

    Castillo, 33, joined the White Sox in a deadline trade with the Seattle Mariners. He struggled badly after the deal, allowing 30 runs in 31 innings, and he finished the season on the injured list with a shoulder concern. Castillo has one year remaining on his contract at $22.75 million, though a $25 million option for 2028 will vest if he throws 150 innings in 2027.

    According to recent reports, the 29-year-old Martin threw 146 innings with a 3.95 ERA in 2026, but it was a 3.41 ERA in the first half and a 5.12 ERA in the second half. The White Sox kept him at arm's length in the postseason despite running bullpen games almost nightly. Martin allowed two runs in one inning in his only postseason appearance.

    Neither Sullivan nor Veliz are significant prospects. For all intents and purposes, the White Sox are attaching Martin to Castillo as a sweetener to get the Rockies to take Castillo's salary. The Rockies are essentially buying Martin, who is under team control through 2030, by taking on the rest of Castillo's contract.

    Here now are our trade grades for this two-for-two swap.

    It has been revealed that fair or not, I'm going to lump the two Castillo trades together. Chicago stepped out to acquire Castillo at the deadline and absorbed the $30 million or so remaining on his contract to do it. Seranthony Domínguez, who had about $15 million left on his deal, went the other way in the trade, so the White Sox took on about $15 million total, and also gave up a pretty good prospect in Boston Smith.

    Four and a half months later, the White Sox had to give up a steady back-end starter in Martin to clear Castillo's money. They ended up saving about $7 million in 2027 in this series of moves, but it cost them Martin and Smith (and Domínguez), and they had to endure 31 awful innings from Castillo. Unless Sullivan or Veliz hit major, the White Sox took a series of Ls here.

    Credit to president of baseball operations Chris Getz for acknowledging a mistake with Castillo and acting quickly to unload him. It was costly, though. Martin isn't a star, but cheap back-end starters are very valuable. We'll see what Getz & Co. do with the savings. Presumably they'll invest in more pitching. Having to give up Martin to dump Castillo so soon is a stinker, though. Ouch.

    Industry observers note that the Rockies need all types of pitching (righty, lefty, starter, reliever, whatever) and it's not often they can convince quality (or even competent) free agents to come to Coors Field. They have to develop their own pitchers or trade for pitching, and in this instance, they took on Castillo's hefty salary to get Martin and his four years of control. Creative, if nothing else.

    Recent findings suggest that there is downside potential too. Martin has run below league-average strikeout rates and middling ground ball rates throughout his career. Pitchers who allow a lot of balls in play -- a lot of balls in play in the air -- are a poor match for Coors Field. It's good the Rockies spent and found a way to add controllable pitching. They just might not have picked the best pitcher.

    Industry observers note that after losing 104 games in 2026, there is no such thing as a bad dart throw for the Rockies. It's unlikely they would have been able to spend the $22.75 million on a free agent (at least not without overpaying), so taking on Castillo to get Martin is the next best thing. I like the thinking, even if I don't love Martin's profile in Coors Field.

    #108377. Paul George embracing role as second option to Jayson Tatum: 'Not one of those guys that have to have an ego'
