    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Published: 12:00 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 04:24 EST, 20 November 2026.

    It has been revealed that the man parked up in a nondescript green Ford Fiesta cut an incongruous sight in the affluent residential neighbourhood of Casal Palocco, in south-west Rome, but no one paid him much notice. He made no eye contact and at no stage stepped from the car.

    It was only after the street’s famous resident, AS Roma’s Belgian midfielder Radja Nainggolan, had his home burgled and an extraordinary £400,000 worth of possessions stolen that the player’s then wife, Claudia, six months pregnant at that time in April 2016, recalled the Eastern European-looking man in the battered vehicle up their street.

    He was Vlada Djuric, a 50-year-old Macedonian of Romani descent and part of the wider Nikolov family, including his wife Zora Jovanovic, their two sons and daughter, whose highly organised thefts from the homes of top footballers would continue for more than a decade, with imprisonment deemed only a minor setback.

    While the Nainggolans were blithely unaware of the criminal family’s lookout man – they’d gone to visit friends nearby for a couple of hours and hadn't even bothered to activate the burglar alarm – the assailants were primed to seize the chance.

    The two sons, Valentino and Giacomo, mounted the villa’s perimeter wall, opening one door with a magnetic card and jimmying another with a screwdriver, and proceeded undisturbed through the house in 27 minutes, throwing the proceeds of their burglary into a bag as they went.

    There were 15 watches (Rolex, Patek Philippe and others) valued at £250,000 and 20 pieces of jewellery, including a diamond worth £25,000. Security cameras on a landing and in an internal room filmed them but such was their confidence, they only partially covered their faces.

    Former Roma midfielder Radja Nainggolan and his then wife Claudia, who was six months pregnant, were the targets of a burglary in 2016 (Source: Instagram/Claudia_lai_82).

    Nainggolan had an extraordinary £400,000 worth of possessions taken, including 15 watches.

    It was old-fashioned detective work from a local officer, Bruno Failla, which led police to a rambling home at Lurano, a small town six hours drive away in Lombardy, at which the Nikolovs would lavishly entertain other members of the Romani community.

    The watches matched the descriptions of those stolen from the Nainggolans, though it was a necklace with a Roma logo, and the pair of red shoes with Nainggolan's initials, which really gave the game away.

    ‘I ask again for vigilance and watchfulness, please,’ Failla remarked at the time, because this was the fourth time that footballers' properties in Casal Palocco had been targeted in the space of five years. But the challenge of placing footballers in a state of constant vigilance became clear fully seven years on, when another Nainggolan residence, in Antwerp, Belgium, was burgled while his relatives held a party there.

    ‘It is one of the most complicated and consistently challenging parts of our security work,’ one former special forces soldier now providing security for footballers tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘It’s been a significant sector of our work for years now, but the movements of these clients are so public and that’s irresistible to criminals. The wealth is very evident.’.

    One of the sons, Valentino, was jailed for two years in 2016 and other members of his family also did time, but once out, they all set their sights on the Premier League. In 2024, they arrived in the UK via a ferry to Dover from Calais, stopped off in London and made their way north, sleeping in a Ford motorhome and travelling to target homes in a Citroen C3.

    A spree of attacks ensued from them on the homes of Alexander Isak, then a Newcastle player, Wolves’ Matheus Cunha (who has subsequently been burgled again while at Manchester United), Birmingham City’s Neil Etheridge and Leon Bailey, with Aston Villa at the time.

    A number of Premier League clubs, including Liverpool, Everton and United, are known to have appointed their own security teams to provide an around-the-clock presence at the homes of players who are in squads playing away from home – rather than have that in the hands of a range of private operators.

    Some of the top football TV analysts are known to have sought the same security cover outside their houses when away at games.

    A number of Premier League clubs, including Liverpool, have appointed their own security teams to provide an around-the-clock presence at the homes of stars who are playing away.

    Three masked criminals managed to slip over Bruno Fernandes' security fence and into his home in Nether Alderley, Cheshire, last month and made off with jewellery.

    In a recent development, it didn’t work in the case of Manchester United’s Bruno Fernandes. Three masked criminals still managed to slip over the security fence into his home in Nether Alderley, Cheshire, last month and make off with jewellery.

    In a recent development, it was one of the player’s neighbours who spotted them on their CCTV system and alerted police, who arrived five minutes after the burglars had left. Some in this security sector feel that it takes the private firms' former military and special services experience to cope with the criminal gangs’ level of sophistication.

    Clubs using security staff in this way is a relatively recent development. In the days of security officers like United’s Ned Kelly, who wrote a book about his 14 years with the club, the job entailed ensuring the team were protected in public, or ferrying managers and newly introduced signings around.

    Many clubs still leave it to players. ‘Player-liaison staff will recommend vetted security providers but it’s down to player personal choice for obvious reasons,’ says one player agent.

    In a recent development, 'That's not always been easy,' says a former Premier League player-liaison officer. 'The players have a huge entourage: so-called experts who want a seat at the table and think they know best. Of course, social media enhances the security problem.'.

    The house burglars’ modus operandi pales by comparison with some of violence displayed by others who prey on the footballer set. One footballer's wife in Cheshire was driving a top-of-the-range vehicle when a moped took up a position in front of her and slowed. In her rear-view mirror, she saw a second. The driver of the third then arrived at her side window, assessing what there was to steal.

    Sources indicate that on any given day, there could have been £200,000 worth of jewellery in the car, though she was wearing neither rings nor a watch on this occasion. The three drove off.

    The episode had echoes of the attempted heist which saw Arsenal’s Mesut Ozil and Sead Kolasinac carjacked in broad daylight in north London, seven years ago.

    It has been revealed that sead Kolasinac, then of Arsenal, thwarts an attempted carjacking in broad daylight in north London, seven years ago. Kolasinac was with his team-mate Mesut Ozil at the time.

    Attackers go for Kolasinac after his car was 'boxed in' when approaching traffic lights.

    Paul Hughes, managing director of Benchmark Security Group, a leading Manchester-based protection firm, employs former police and Royal security drivers to train his clients in the art of 'defensive driving'.

    In a two-hour session, they learn how to avoid being 'boxed in' – as Ozil and Kolasinac were – when approaching traffic lights. Techniques include never taking up a position in the middle lane, avoiding the outside lane if there is a central barrier, and always maintaining sight of the tyres of the vehicle in front when you slow.

    'If you can see the tyres, you will always have room to manoeuvre right or left of the car in front, at speed, without hitting it,' Hughes says.

    Sources indicate that his staff are often asked to escort clients in their fleet of vehicles, which includes two Land Rovers with blacked-out windows. Escorted school runs are also part of the protection they offer.

    A screen which dominates Benchmark's underground headquarters, at anonymous premises in Manchester, revealed the fortresses that players' houses have become, when I visited.

    According to recent reports, it showed live feeds from the gardens of mansions which are criss-crossed by infra-red beams. An alarm is triggered in the control room if anyone not approved through face-recognition software is picked up by up to 18 pan, tilt and zoom cameras at a property.

    It has been revealed that loudspeakers, operated from the control room, warn off intruders. A team of security staff is never more than six minutes away. A patrol is on the scene of an alert, usually within 90 seconds.

    Recent findings suggest that A number of Manchester United players have invested in specialised security dogs from the Leicester-based firm Chaperone K9 at a cost of up to £20,000 each, though some sources suggest demand has receded as many players have young children. Security firms have their own dogs.

    Industry observers note that benchmark are one of Britain's most trusted operators – industry-accredited, with former senior police officers on their staff. But this is also a world in which some unsavoury individuals are looking to extract gain.

    According to recent reports, daily Mail Sport is aware that a number of current players have paid protection money to ensure they remain safe and are not venturing out socially without having done so. The ‘panic rooms’ some install in their homes, with security card access, are a place to hide valuables.

    According to recent reports, the family who preyed on footballers for a decade will be behind bars for some time. Valentino Nikolov (pictured) is serving an initial 10-year sentence, which has since been extended.

    Industry observers note that kolasinac fought off the carjackers. Everton's Duncan Ferguson put an assailant in hospital when he tried to burgle his home at Ormskirk, Lancashire, in January 2001. ‘I’m not a hard man off the pitch...unless you try to break into my house,’ he mentioned recently.

    But the assailants in the Ozil and Kolasinac attack were part of Eastern European gangs. 'The criminal demographic has changed,' one former senior detective tells me. 'We are now talking about gangs who lack the slightest compunction about taking a life.'.

    The Italian family who have preyed on footballers for a decade will be behind bars for some time. The Rome lookout man’s two sons were jailed for 10 years and eight years respectively at Newcastle Crown Court last year, for burglaries including the Isak attack – sentences since extended. Their mother is doing seven years.

    That court case revealed how the family had moved on from the days of old cars, screwdrivers and shinning over walls in Rome – using Isak’s own vehicle as a battering ram to force entry to his Newcastle home.

    Arsenal will host old nemesis José Mourinho’s Real Madrid in the league phase of the Champions League.

    Mourinho, the former Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur manager, will return to London to resume hostilities against last season’s beaten finalists.

    Other reunions from Thursday’s draw include Manchester City travelling to Barcelona, to whom they last week sold Rodri, and Liverpool visiting Inter Milan, who have signed Curtis Jones.

    Mourinho last managed at the Emirates Stadium in March 2021, barely a month before his sacking by Spurs.

    During his two spells as Chelsea manager, Mourinho famously had run-ins with Arsenal’s Arsène Wenger.

    Mourinho called Wenger a “specialist in failure” after the Frenchman failed to add to his three Premier League titles following his Portuguese counterpart’s arrival in London in 2004.

    Last season, Mikel Arteta finally ended Arsenal’s long wait to be crowned champions of England but agonisingly missed out on European glory.

    Sources indicate that verdict Premier League champions should not be daunted by any game, but Real Madrid – with Mourinho in control – has the feel of a defining match of the group stage.     Verdict Playing against the European champions and travelling to Barcelona will be a true test of how much progress Enzo Maresca has made in the short time he has been at the Etihad Stadium.     Recent findings suggest that verdict The repeat of the 1999 final is the standout fixture, but Michael Carrick should be looking beyond that match for the points needed to progress. He has been given a tough set of away games to navigate. They are winnable but difficult. So those games at Old Trafford will be very crucial.

    The top eight teams of the league phase progress to the last 16 automatically, while teams that finish between ninth and 24th will be forced to navigate a play-off tie to reach the knockout stages.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Coming off a disaster of a season and with a roster badly in need of an overhaul, the Giants make sense as a team to make a trade or two this offseason.
    • In a recent development, webb, 30, has two years and $47 million left on his current deal.
    • It has been revealed that which teams might make for a good fit for Webb?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Coming off a disaster of a season and with a roster badly in need of an overhaul, the Giants make sense as a team to make a trade or two this offseason. Sure enough, they are "listening to trade offers" for All-Star starting pitcher Logan Webb, per The Athletic, but they'd need a "very strong return" in order to deal him.

    In a recent development, webb, 30, has two years and $47 million left on his current deal. He went 8-9 with a 4.31 ERA and 1.3 WAR last season, but it was his worst year in quite a while. He averaged 4.5 WAR per season in the previous four years with a 3.22 ERA and led the National League in innings pitched from 2023 to 2025, racking up three straight top-six Cy Young finishes.

    It has been revealed that which teams might make for a good fit for Webb? Many of them. We're talking about a workhorse under team control for two more years. Let's run through five of the best fits while, again, knowing that basically any contender should be interested in at least a conversation with the Giants.

    The Cubs need so much pitching this offseason. Their entire rotation heading into the playoffs last season is in free agency. This isn't hyperbole. Matthew Boyd, Shota Imanaga, Kevin Gausman, Clay Holmes and David Peterson are all off the roster. If the Cubs were to try and put together a rotation right now, it would be something like Justin Steele, Edward Cabrera, Javier Assad and several question marks. Ben Brown and Cade Horton will open the season on the injured list.

    Industry observers note that do we really need to spell out what a reliable innings eater would mean for this bunch? Webb is an outstanding fit here.

    It has been revealed that the upstart playoff team last season was a ton of fun, but also was running bullpen games in the ALDS. The White Sox just attached Davis Martin to Luis Castillo in a trade to the Rockies in order to offload Castillo's contract, too, so they're down a starter. The Dustin May signing means they have him along with Sean Burke and converted reliever Grant Taylor. The White Sox would reportedly like to sign another starter in the May ballpark, but what about trading for someone better like Webb?

    A top four in the rotation of Webb, Burke, Taylor and May would be exponentially better than what the Sox had last season.

    Returns of Spencer Strider and Spencer Schwellenbach at some point will help, but this is still a thin rotation for a team coming off a division title. Chris Sale remains, but he's followed up with Grant Holmes and Bryce Elder before the Spencers return. Youngster Didier Fuentes moving to the rotation is exciting, but there are an awful lot of questions behind Sale, who turns 38 in late March, by the way.

    According to recent reports, given that the Padres reside in the NL West with the Giants, there might be a bit of an intradivision tax in terms of the asking price, but Padres boss A.J. Preller is never shy about offloading prospects. There could certainly be a fit. The Padres need rotation help, too, after losing Michael King, Nick Pivetta, Robbie Ray and others to free agency. We know they're in on Tarik Skubal, but that doesn't mean they'll be content with just landing one major fish.

    Look at the current Padres rotation. It's basically Joe Musgrove and Randy Vásquez. With three straight playoff berths and zero trips to the World Series, now isn't the time to have Jhony Brito, Ryan Weiss and Ian Koenig make up 60% of the rotation.

    Dealing for Webb and signing Skubal would make for a nice offseason for upcoming ownership, no?

    One of the most disappointing teams in baseball last season needs to have a prolific offseason. We've heard plenty about the Mets being involved in the Skubal sweepstakes and we've seen them win a monster bidding war before (see: Soto, Juan). Grabbing Webb would make it quite a well-rounded rotation with talented youngsters Nolan McLean, Christian Scott and Zac Thornton.

    Hello football friends, and welcome to the Monday edition of the Pick Six newsletter!

    It is officially Thanksgiving week, and if you're an NFL fan, that means you should probably just go ahead and clear your schedule from now until the end of the month because there is going to be an NFL game on almost every day.

    That means there will be at least one game in six of the next eight days. Is that more football than I need? Probably, but I always eat more turkey than I need on Thanksgiving and never regret it, so I don't think I'll regret it if I watch every game between now and Nov. 30.

    You also won't regret reading today's newsletter, so let's get to the rundown.

    Welcome to my favorite part of the Monday newsletter: The part where I hand out grades for every team that played. The easiest grade to hand out this week went to the 49ers, who destroyed the Vikings in an NFC Showdown. The 49ers spent the entire week practicing in Colorado to get prepared for the 7,350-foot elevation in Mexico City, and it definitely indicated.

    With that in mind, let's get to a few of the grades from Week 11:.

    As for the other grades that we've handed out so far in Week 11, you can check those out here.

    You can't have a week of NFL action without winners and losers, so here are some of them. Carter Bahns put together this week's list of winners and losers, and we'll check out his losers below. It was such an ugly week for the Steelers that he actually put them down twice on this list.

    If you want to see Carter's list of winners (and a couple of other losers), be sure to click here.

    Sources indicate that everyone on the internet loves to overreact, and that's especially true when we're talking about the NFL. Zach Pereles looked at several things that happened during Week 11, so decide for yourself whether we're all overreacting.

    It has been revealed that statement: Jesse Minter will be one-and-done in Baltimore.Overreaction or reality: Overreaction. Lots of the Ravens' concerns are out of first-year coach Jesse Minter's control. The Lamar Jackson injuries, obviously, threw the season way off course. Even Sunday's game was another example of the things Minter can't control going wrong. Justice Hill fumbled 1 yard from the end zone. LaJohntay Wester muffed two punts, one of which the Panthers recovered. Derrick Henry also lost a fumble. It's been a season from hell. But there are plenty of issues Minter has been responsible for — or at least hasn't fixed — this year. Regarded as a defensive whiz after two years as the Chargers' defensive coordinator, he now oversees a defense that ranks in the bottom half of the league in yards per game and yards per play, and in the bottom 10 in yards per pass attempt and takeaways. Simply put, it's been underwhelming at best for a team expected to contend for a championship. But the Ravens won't fire Minter at season's end. There are big-picture questions about Jackson and the entire roster, but Minter should get an offseason to tweak and improve his defense and fit it better to his defenders.

    Statement: The Buccaneers have a serious Baker Mayfield problem.Overreaction or reality: Reality. The Buccaneers extended Mayfield with a three-year, $165 million deal just before the season began, after it seemed like an extension wouldn't happen. Tampa Bay must be wishing it hadn't made the deal. Mayfield is constantly banged up - he's dealing with plantar fasciitis in addition to the thumb injury that caused him to miss several games already this year - and he can't physically make his play style work. How the Buccaneers overcome this is TBD, because there are no realistic easy answers.

    Statement: Jahmyr Gibbs will win Offensive Player of the Year. Overreaction or reality: Reality. It wasn't always pretty, but Jahmyr Gibbs ground out 118 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns in the Lions' 31-21 win over the Buccaneers. He's up to 1,502 yards from scrimmage this season and on pace to finish with 2,553. That would break Chris Johnson's all-time record of 2,509 from 2009. That, one would think, would clinch an Offensive Player of the Year award for Gibbs. Even if he doesn't break the record, Gibbs would be a deserving winner, so long as he keeps producing. He's had at least 110 yards from scrimmage in all but two games.

    • Here in Major League Baseball news, that normally means we're bound for a slow week -- save for a few notable exceptions -- but with the CBA expiring on Dec.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Welcome to Thanksgiving week. Here in Major League Baseball news, that normally means we're bound for a slow week -- save for a few notable exceptions -- but with the CBA expiring on Dec. 1, we might just be in for a free agent frenzy. Let's hope that's the case.

    We can start today's set of news and rumors with the biggest free agent out there.

    Tarik Skubal is the No. 1 free agent this offseason and the two-time Cy Young winner appears on pace to make a decision before the CBA expires. Skubal's agent, Scott Boras, hit MLB Network Radio on Sunday and remarked that there's a "strong likelihood" that a decision comes by that Dec. 1 deadline, especially given that Skubal's signing impacts so many other pitchers (Boras mentioned that it impacts "10-15 pitchers").

    The 30-year-old lefty was 12-7 with a 2.72 ERA and 186 strikeouts in 158 ⅔ innings last season, as he bounced back after just six weeks from elbow surgery.

    The teams most heavily involved in the Skubal rumors to this point have been the Dodgers, Mets, Padres and Blue Jays, all of whom had in-person meetings with him last week.

    The Tigers have agreed to a deal with right-hander Luis Gil, per ESPN. It's a one-year, $2.3 million deal.

    Gil won the American League Rookie of the Year after a productive 2024 season in which he won 15 games and had a 3.50 ERA, but he spent a good portion of 2026 in the minors and was nontendered by the Yankees on Friday. In his limited MLB time last season, Gil had a 4.61 ERA, 1.43 WHIP and 17 strikeouts in 27 ⅓ innings.

    The Tigers rotation seems set with Framber Valdez, Troy Melton, Keider Montero, Jackson Jobe and River Ryan, so consider Gil a depth option.

    The Red Sox also reportedly highlighted interest.

    #108338. Breaking: Kyrie Irving to the Jazz? Why Utah's reported interest in the star Mavericks guard makes no sense

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1440 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Kyrie Irving to the Jazz? Why Utah's reported interest in the star Mavericks guard makes no sense

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1440 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that NBA teams are remarkably diligent.
    • In a recent development, on Thursday, one such rumor arrived as SNY's Ian Begley reported that the Utah Jazz have given Kyrie Irving "internal consideration as a potential trade candidate." Now, this is common.
    • In a recent development, so, let's consider this rumor in earnest.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that NBA teams are remarkably diligent. They will consider almost any path to improving their rosters, no matter how obscure or unexpected. Still, every now and then, a truly bizarre nugget hits the rumor mill and forces us to consider what exactly a team is thinking.

    In a recent development, on Thursday, one such rumor arrived as SNY's Ian Begley reported that the Utah Jazz have given Kyrie Irving "internal consideration as a potential trade candidate." Now, this is common. Teams will do due diligence on a wide variety of players leading up to transaction periods in order to make sure they've covered their bases, and Begley gives no indication that there have even been talks between the Jazz and the Dallas Mavericks. Still, as he notes, "you're not gonna spend a lot of time on a player if you don't have any interest in him, so the idea of Utah spending some time internally on Kyrie Irving was interesting.".

    In a recent development, so, let's consider this rumor in earnest. The Jazz entered this season with playoff expectations after four straight years in the lottery. They are 3-13 due to a combination of injuries, players adjusting to a latest roster and simply poor performance. Utah has shown a willingness to trade for players outside of its perceived timeline before. The Jazz looked at then-33-year-old Jrue Holiday early in their rebuild in 2023, for instance, but backed off when Holiday's camp reportedly made it clear he would not be interested in extending.

    According to recent reports, irving, still a star-caliber scorer, has the Mavericks at 8-7 through 15 games. He's averaging over 22 points on roughly his standard efficiency for a Dallas team with pretty limited shooting around him. We can't say at this stage whether or not the Mavericks are willing to trade him. The notion that they might depends on the team's asset deficit (Dallas does not control its own first-round pick again until 2031) and the 15-year age gap between Irving and franchise player Cooper Flagg, but Dallas could easily elect to simply build off this early success.

    Recent findings suggest that if they do take the long view and consider trade offers, Irving could absolutely help a team trying to win right now. Plenty of teams potentially looking for individual shot-creation, like the Detroit Pistons, Houston Rockets and Miami Heat, could be planning pursuits of the future Hall of Famer.

    It has been revealed that the question here is why the Jazz, specifically, would be interested in Irving, because on paper, there is perhaps not a single, high-profile player who makes less sense for this roster than he does. Utah's young core revolves around three perimeter players: Keyonte George, Darryn Peterson and Ace Bailey. The Jazz are so strong on that front that Bailey came off the bench to start the season, and it's unclear how exactly they initiative to handle their starting five when Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. return from injuries. If Utah isn't comfortable with Jackson playing center full time, and the Memphis Grizzlies certainly weren't, then one of those five players either needs to get traded or come off the bench.

    According to recent reports, adding Irving to this logjam doesn't make sense. Neither does trading one of those players for Irving. George is 23. Bailey is 20. Peterson is 19. Teams that are 10 games below .500 simply don't trade foundational pieces for players a decade or more their senior. They gave up three first-round picks for Jackson largely to improve their defense, and now that Walker Kessler plays for the Los Angeles Lakers, his presence matters more than ever.

    According to recent reports, markkanen is the obvious trade candidate of the group, but he's still five years younger than Irving and plays a less saturated position. If Utah viewed Markkanen's max contract as a negative it needed to escape, that would be one thing, but there's just no evidence at this stage that this is the case. They have rebuffed trade interest in Markkanen at every turn. If Dallas were willing to put substantial draft equity on the table to cover the age and positional gaps here, there could perhaps be a conversation, but Dallas isn't in a position to do so.

    There's some merit to the idea that Utah might eventually want to shake up its backcourt. There were rumors during the draft process that Peterson's representatives were skeptical of Utah as a landing spot because they also represent George and felt that two score-first guards would clash. Even if the Jazz were prepared to split them up less than 20 games into Peterson's career, Irving himself has typically fared far better when he has been paired with a high-level passer. He won his championship with LeBron James. He's thriving next to Cooper Flagg now. His best trait is, and always has been, his scoring.

    And then, of course, there is the history shared between Irving and Utah's top executive. The CEO of the Jazz is Danny Ainge, who once traded for Irving when he ran the Boston Celtics. Before his second season in Boston, Irving publicly shared aims to re-sign with the Celtics as a free agent in 2019. When the time came, he instead joined the Brooklyn Nets, a divisional opponent. This is the NBA. If LeBron James can reunite with Dan Gilbert, any player-executive reunion is theoretically possible. Nonetheless, Ainge and Irving would seemingly be among the unlikeliest pairings in all of basketball. Put all of this together and this is a puzzling rumor to say the least.

    Sometimes a rumor says more about a team's big-picture looks than it does a specific target. For a variety of reasons, some of which we've covered, it seems exceedingly unlikely that the Jazz are going to trade for Irving. However, they've invested the time in considering it, as Begley noted. That means something, even if it doesn't mean a trade is coming.

    Sources indicate that the simplest read on this is that Utah is concerned enough about its short-term prospects that it is considering investing in win-now help despite its 3-13 start. That, in itself, makes sense. The Jazz don't control their own first-round pick this season. They have no incentive to lose, and while making the postseason despite starting the season 10 games under .500 is improbable, it just happened a year ago when the 4-14 Charlotte Hornets recovered quickly enough to reach the Play-In Tournament. The Jazz are 5.5 games out of the No. 10 seed in the Western Conference right now. If they get healthy in time and make the right addition, perhaps they could still make a real run at it.

    It has been revealed that skepticism about the George-Peterson fit, for now, should be on the back burner. Though the two fared far better early on when they played separately, both, at least for now, have better net ratings and true shooting percentages in the minutes they've shared than the minutes they haven't. George's usage skyrockets when he plays without Peterson, but that's to be expected with Markkanen and Jackson out.

    There may have been concern early in the season, and that might have been when Irving crossed Utah's mind. There may still be concerns down the line when the Jazz have had a longer sample size to evaluate the pairing with the rest of their roster. For now, though, it's simply too early to consider splitting up such a talented tandem, especially right as the team has actually started winning some games.

    However, ball-handling behind them is a valid concern. Utah declined its fourth-year option on backup point guard and former first-round pick Isaiah Collier, and the offense has been 6.5 points per 100 possessions worse with him on the floor this season. Adding a veteran backup point guard, if only to ease Peterson's burden during the minutes George rests, would be sensible. Irving is obviously no backup, but as perhaps the most notable point guard theoretically on the market, it makes sense that the Jazz would at least broach the concept internally.

    Ainge hasn't earned the nickname "Trader Danny" for nothing. His teams are almost always at the center of the trade market, and as last year's Jackson deal proved, he's as capable of a stunner as he's ever been. Irving would certainly qualify as one. We shouldn't expect it. It wouldn't really make sense based on what we know now. But in the post-Luka Dončić trade NBA, it would be hard to dismiss basically any rumor involving a player of this stature.

    Dylan Larkin trade grades: Red Wings notch massive win in blockbuster NHL deal with Canadiens

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (880 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that the Detroit Red Wings have traded former captain Dylan Larkin to the Montreal Canadiens in a blockbuster trade, the teams declared on Sunday.
    • According to recent reports, in addition to Larkin, Detroit sent a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick to Montreal.
    • According to recent reports, larkin requested a trade back in June, and his relationship with the Red Wings only grew more acrimonious with each passing day.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that the Detroit Red Wings have traded former captain Dylan Larkin to the Montreal Canadiens in a blockbuster trade, the teams declared on Sunday. This deal ends a bitter saga between Larkin and the Red Wings, and Montreal gave up a king's ransom to make it happen.

    According to recent reports, in addition to Larkin, Detroit sent a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick to Montreal. The Red Wings received forward Kirby Dach, goaltender Sam Montembeault, prospect Michael Hage, first-round picks in 2027 and 2029, a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fourth-round pick.

    According to recent reports, larkin requested a trade back in June, and his relationship with the Red Wings only grew more acrimonious with each passing day. As training camp opened in September, Detroit announced that Larkin had been stripped of his captaincy, and Larkin was booed by fans on opening night at Little Caesars Arena.

    After recovering from an injury he suffered in camp, Larkin played 10 games before announcing that he would be sitting out in anticipation of the trade. While sitting out, Larkin racked up major fines, but his trade request has finally been granted.

    Industry observers note that when he's on the ice, there's no denying that Larkin can make a significant impact. The 30-year-old Larkin just notched 34 goals and 33 assists for the Red Wings last season -- his fifth straight year hitting the 30-goal mark -- and he was instrumental in Team USA ending its lengthy gold medal drought at the 2026 Olympics.

    Industry observers note that in his career, Larkin has totaled 278 goals and 371 assists in 818 games. The first game Larkin — a native of Waterford, Michigan — plays for the Habs will also be the first he's ever played for a team based outside the Wolverine State.

    Larkin will give the Canadiens much-needed center depth, and he'll be under contract for a while. He's in the fourth year of an eight-year contract that pays him $8.7 million per season.

    In a recent development, this trade fills a void that's existed in the Canadiens' lineup for several years now. Nick Suzuki has evolved into a legitimate star and a franchise-caliber No. 1 center. Beyond him, Montreal has struggled to find a true second-line center.

    According to recent reports, larkin absolutely fits that bill. While he was a bit miscast in Detroit as a first-line center, Larkin is one of the best No. 2 options in the NHL, and he gives the Canadiens an elite one-two punch down the middle.

    Did the Canadiens overpay a bit for a 30-year-old second-line center? In a vacuum, they did. However, taken in context, this deal makes plenty of sense for the Habs.

    Industry observers note that montreal's championship window is just now opening. It already has an elite young core locked up for the next several seasons on team-friendly deals. Suzuki, Cole Caufield, Ivan Demidov, Juraj Slafkovsky, Lane Hutson and Noah Dobson are all 27 or younger and make less than $10 million per season.

    That gives general manager Kent Hughes a bit more freedom to be aggressive on the trade market. Picks and prospects are nice, but they don't do much good for a team looking to make the jump to contender status in 2026-27. Besides, the Canadiens have been building their prospect pool for years now. It's time to flip some of those assets for proven star power.

    The Canadiens paid a premium to acquire Larkin. There's no two ways about it. However, Montreal fills a major need and looks a lot more formidable in the Eastern Conference. The Stanley Cup window is officially wide open for the ascending Canadiens. Grade -- B+.

    Consider the situation interim general manager Shawn Horcoff faced. Everyone knew that Larkin wanted out of Detroit so badly that he was paying not to play for the Red Wings.

    On top of that, Larkin had a full no-trade clause, and his list of approved teams amounted to no more than a dozen.

    Should I also mention that Horcoff was thrust into this role in the midst of the offseason, when franchise legend Steve Yzerman was effectively fired for mishandling the Wings' rebuild?

    Sources indicate that given all of that, it's hard to see this as anything less than a home run for Detroit. In fact, it's probably more like a grand slam. Not only did the Red Wings get multiple first-round picks and a couple useful NHL players out of the deal, but they also landed a legitimate blue-chip prospect in Hage.

    Recent findings suggest that the No. 21 pick in the 2024 NHL Draft, Hage is off to a roaring start at the University of Michigan this season with five goals and 21 assists in just 13 games. Detroit might have replaced one franchise center with another one, assuming Hage continues to develop at this rate.

    This was a great piece of work from Horcoff, who probably just made a strong case for the full-time general manager gig in Detroit. This haul will allow the Wings to kickstart another retool or swing a big trade to bolster the current roster. Either way, the outlook just got a lot brighter in Hockeytown. Grade -- A+.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Brandon Aiyuk's time in San Francisco has apparently come to an end.
    • The 49ers were given a two-week roster exemption when the NFL reinstated Aiyuk on Nov.
    • Aiyuk started the 2025 season on the PUP list.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Brandon Aiyuk's time in San Francisco has apparently come to an end. The 49ers have released Aiyuk, who will now look to continue his career with a upcoming team, according to a report from ESPN.

    The 49ers were given a two-week roster exemption when the NFL reinstated Aiyuk on Nov. 9. With that exemption ending on Nov. 23, the 49ers elected to move on from Aiyuk, who hasn't played an NFL game since tearing his ACL and MCL during the 2024 season. Aiyuk had signed a four-year, $120 deal with the 49ers that offseason following a tumultuous negotiation. That contract, as presently structured, still has two years remaining, with a 2027 cap hit of $40.5 million according to Over the Cap, meaning Aiyuk will likely need to clear waivers before any team formally signs him.

    Aiyuk started the 2025 season on the PUP list. That November, it was reported that the 49ers voided the guaranteed money in his contract for 2026 due to lack of participation. In December, the 49ers placed him on their reserve/left squad list.

    This summer, the 49ers placed Aiyuk on the reserve/did not report list (meaning the 49ers were not obligated to pay him and he did not count against their roster) after he did not report to training camp. Aiyuk had since applied for reinstatement with the NFL and was granted it earlier this month.

    Before 2024, Aiyuk enjoyed a productive career with the 49ers, who selected him with the 25th overall pick in the 2020 draft. In 2022, he eclipsed 1,000 receiving yards for the first time and caught a career-high eight touchdowns. The following season, he recorded a career-high 1,342 receiving yards while helping the 49ers reach the Super Bowl.

    Industry observers note that while his recent actions in San Francisco might scare some teams off, Aiyuk will likely draw interest from teams that need help at receiver. Aiyuk has long been linked to the Commanders; he and Washington quarterback Jayden Daniels were teammates at Arizona State. The Steelers are another team that could potentially be a landing spot for Aiyuk.

    It has been revealed that despite not having Aiyuk, the 49ers are 9-1 and would be the No. 1 seed in the NFL if the playoffs started today.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, ace left-hander Tarik Skubal, winner of the last two American League Cy Young awards and far and away the top free agent of the 2026-27 class, has agreed to terms with the Fresh York Mets on a nine-year contract worth $450 million, reports the New York Post. The deal has a $45 million signing bonus with no options or opt-outs, per SNY, as well as a full no-trade clause, so the Mets have locked Skubal up for the full nine years. Further, there are only $30 million in deferrals, according to the New York Post. The deal is pending a physical.

    Once finalized, the deal will make Skubal the highest-paid pitcher in Major League Baseball history, in terms of both total contract value and average annual salary.

    According to recent reports, skubal, who turned 30 years of age on Nov. 20, is the No. 1 ranked talent on our list of the top 50 free agents for this offseason. Here's part of Mike Axisa's write-up:.

    Industry observers note that "Excluding Yoshinobu Yamamoto, who was a special case as a Japanese star with no MLB track record, Skubal is the best starting pitcher to hit free agency since Gerrit Cole in 2019. He showed few long-lasting effects from the NanoScope elbow surgery in May and remains a capital-A Ace with terrific surface stats and under-the-hood performance indicators. Skubal brings four swing-and-miss pitches to the table (four-seamer, changeup, slider, curveball), a near MLB-best ability to limit exit velocity, and elite strike-throwing ability (MLB's third-lowest walk rate since 2023). Build an ace starter in a lab and he would look a lot like Skubal. He'll play the entire 2027 season at age 30, and given the things teams can do with pitchers these days, Skubal figures to remain a frontline starter for most of a long-term contract. He's the only true balance-of-power player available in free agency this offseason. Skubal can swing a division race and a postseason series all by himself.".

    In a recent development, over the last three seasons, Skubal has pitched to a 2.42 ERA and an FIP of 2.48 in 546 innings spread over 88 starts. That amounts to a total WAR of 17.7 since the start of the 2024 campaign. Skubal remains foremost in the discussion for best pitcher in baseball, and this signing reflects that reality.

    Since Skubal was traded to the Los Angeles Dodgers from the Detroit Tigers leading up to the 2026 deadline, he was ineligible to receive the qualifying offer from the Dodgers. As such, the Mets will not be penalized a draft pick for signing Skubal.

    The nine years here aren't record-setting, as the longest pitcher contract remains the 12-year deal that Yoshinobu Yamamoto signed with the Dodgers. Yamamoto's $325 million was previously the largest contract for a pitcher -- obviously excepting Shohei Ohtani, as he's a two-way player -- so Skubal's $450 million shatters that record.

    According to recent reports, coming off a disappointing 88-loss campaign in 2026, the Mets, substantial-spending owner Steve Cohen, and lead decision-maker David Stearns needed to make an offseason splash to improve their chances of a 2027 rebound and inspire a perhaps disaffected fan base. Skubal more than qualifies. He'll front a Mets rotation that also includes 25-year-old right-hander Nolan McLean, who himself has frontline long-term potential. In Queens, Skubal joins a roster that also includes the All-Star likes of Juan Soto, Francisco Lindor, and Bo Bichette.

    It has been revealed that further, the Mets just locked up young outfielder A.J. Ewing to an eight-year, $95 million extension and we all know plenty about Soto's monster contract. The Mets now have Soto through 2039, Skubal through 2035, Ewing through 2034 and Lindor through 2031.

    The rotation for the Mets right now looks something like:.

    It has been revealed that given the large outlay for Skubal here, the Mets should be all-in on improving the ballclub for the 2027 season, which means we shouldn't expect them to stop with just signing Skubal.     #108333. Tech Report: Inside Newcastle United's transfer tension: Matthias Jaissle wants greater control as he eyes a new No 10 and No 9 in January - but the next four fixtures could make or break him and the club's season, writes CRAIG HOPE

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (969 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: Inside Newcastle United's transfer tension: Matthias Jaissle wants greater control as he eyes a new No 10 and No 9 in January - but the next four fixtures could make or break him and the club's season, writes CRAIG HOPE

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (969 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Published: 12:49 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 05:54 EST, 20 November 2026.
    • This time, Matthias Jaissle wants his fingerprints on the bank notes.
    • Industry observers note that the need for reinforcement is clear, even on the back of £270million invested in the summer.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

    Published: 12:49 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 05:54 EST, 20 November 2026.

    This time, Matthias Jaissle wants his fingerprints on the bank notes. But what the head coach wishes for in January, and what Newcastle United are willing and able to give, is likely to be very different. When that happens, it rarely ends well - on the pitch or off it.

    Industry observers note that the need for reinforcement is clear, even on the back of £270million invested in the summer. Jaissle knows as much and is not afraid to say so. The rookie German has to protect himself as much as he does his club.

    In a recent development, because, as Newcastle prepare for what threatens to be a long and testing winter, Jaissle is revisiting the brochure presented to him in the summer. And that is the 38-year-old's concern and frustration - the prospectus for the season ahead was not of his making.

    In a recent development, he arrived three weeks before the start of the campaign and with four of eight signings already through the door. At a cost of £110m, that quartet have started just three Premier League games between them, and each of those by teenager Sean Steur. Baz Toure and Aladji Bamba are virtual spectators, while reserve keeper Ewen Jaouen is injured.

    For Jaissle, you suspect, that money was not spent as he would have advised, had he been in situ. Now, in the new year, he wants greater control, as well as a No 10 and No 9. For any Newcastle follower averse to tension, you best watch this transfer window through your fingertips.

    Jaissle, sporting director Ross Wilson and chief executive David Hopkinson are the protagonists who will navigate January. At least, that is, if Jaissle makes it into 2027. He deserves that time - not least because of the turbulent and transitional situation he inherited - but the next four fixtures will potentially make or break him and the season.

    Head coach Matthias Jaissle is seeking greater control of Newcastle United's transfer strategy.

    Aladji Bamba has been a virtual spectator and joined in the summer before Jaissle's arrival.

    After the visit of league leaders Arsenal on Saturday, there is a trip to second-placed Brighton, followed by a seismic home double header in the space of five days against Mauricio Pochettino's Manchester United and bitter rivals Sunderland.

    It is why, despite rumblings behind the scenes in recent days of potential transfer discord, Jaissle was on message - the collective, club message - when I asked him about the profile of player he might want in January.

    'It's not the time to talk about the transfer window,' he stated. 'We have players capable to deliver higher performances on the pitch. We have big quality, not only up front, but throughout the whole squad. We believe we can do better and this is what we now want to influence.'.

    Industry observers note that however, there was a softening when I sympathised with the head coach over him being judged by a window for which he did not have ownership. Did he, then, want more influence this time?

    'Now, it's a different story (compared to the summer), if you're already in and also if you have clarified your clear idea, your clear needs, it's going to be easier,' he noted.

    'But the transfer market is still a long time ahead, at least it feels like that right now with our fixtures. Our task, especially from my stance, is to focus on the next match and the upcoming challenges.'.

    Jaissle knows that his case will only be strengthened by a steadying of results, even though, conversely, more defeats would heighten the need for signings. They have lost four from six in all competitions.

    Industry observers note that the problem is that the hierarchy are on the record as stating the summer business went pretty much exactly as they wished and believed they had a squad for the entire season. There are also Squad Cost Ratio limitations. It is understood there is headroom for one player, but not the two the manager would prefer and not at a fee approaching the £51m they paid for Matias Fernandez-Pardo on deadline day.

    Jaissle wants a upcoming No 9 to compete with the likes of Yoane Wisse who has one league goal.

    Matias Fernandez-Pardo (left) has failed to impress so far at Newcastle after his £51m arrival.

    According to recent reports, the 21-year-old forward is another problem. He is still to score from seven appearances and there is a fear he is not yet strong enough for the Premier League. Interestingly, Jaissle revealed on Thursday his dismay that he was booked during the 1-1 draw at Fulham last time out for screaming at Fernandez-Pardo to stand up.

    That is not to say Jaissle does not believe in the talent of those brought in. He does. But for a coach in his first season in a major European league, he needs players who can impact today, not tomorrow. He needs, and wants, more experience. One of his first recommendations in August was to sign 31-year-old midfielder Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg. Nico Gonzalez eventually arrived in that position, but the 24-year-old looks like a player who has spent two seasons in reserve at Manchester City.

    It has been revealed that so, it is easy to see why Jaissle needs and wants more in January. It is also easy to see why he might not get it. There could be trouble ahead, and that is not just the upcoming matches.

    #108331. Connor Bedard injury: Blackhawks star's latest issue shines light on a stalled out rebuild in Chicago

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (927 w)

    General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Connor Bedard injury: Blackhawks star's latest issue shines light on a stalled out rebuild in Chicago

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (927 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • An awful start for the Chicago Blackhawks only got worse on Monday night when the team declared that captain and superstar forward Connor Bedard would miss four months after undergoing right shoulder surgery.
    • According to recent reports, on Nov.
    • Bedard missed the first two weeks of the season while recovering from surgery on his left shoulder in the offseason.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    An awful start for the Chicago Blackhawks only got worse on Monday night when the team declared that captain and superstar forward Connor Bedard would miss four months after undergoing right shoulder surgery.

    According to recent reports, on Nov. 17, Bedard injured his shoulder on a face-off and left the ice in a lot of discomfort. After deliberating whether to rehab the shoulder or get surgery to repair the glitch, Bedard opted for the latter half. That will sideline him longer now, but it could provide a more permanent fix.

    Bedard missed the first two weeks of the season while recovering from surgery on his left shoulder in the offseason. The Blackhawks captain suffered that injury during summer training -- and that also occurred on a seemingly innocuous play.

    It has been revealed that even after Bedard's initial injury, Chicago hoped that the 2026-27 season would be a step in the right direction amid a lengthy rebuild. Instead, the team is on track to finish with fewer points this year than last year -- despite playing two more games.

    The Blackhawks are 8-14-2, which is good for 30th place in the NHL. Only the aging Pittsburgh Penguins and actively tanking Vancouver Canucks sit below them. The prospects Chicago has drafted in recent years haven't shown adequate process at the NHL level, and they've got no veteran support around them.

    With Bedard out for an extended period of time, the Blackhawks must re-assess their long-term vision.

    When healthy, Bedard has shown that he can be a true superstar. The 21-year-old has 82 goals and 139 assists in 234 career games, and he began the 2025-26 season on a torrid pace before, well, suffering a shoulder injury.

    And therein lies the biggest question about Bedard's future as a true force in the NHL. Is this just bad luck, or will his lack of durability prevent him from reaching the potential that's evident when the puck is on his stick? Chicago can only hope its the former, but this isn't the first time Bedard has missed significant time due to injury.

    Industry observers note that this is now Bedard's fourth NHL season, and he's played 70-plus games just once. That was in the 2024-25 season, when he played all 82 games and tallied 67 points.

    Last season, a right shoulder injury forced him to miss 13 games and snuffed out his tremendous start. Months later, Bedard injured his left shoulder after taking a spill during summer workouts. That prompted one surgery, and his latest right shoulder injury prompted another procedure less than five months later.

    I'm certainly not a doctor, but two shoulder surgeries that close together seems concerning, especially for how much the Blackhawks have invested in Bedard.

    Recent findings suggest that in 2022-23, the franchise completely demolished its roster in hopes of landing the No. 1 overall pick. It worked, and Chicago got to draft Bedard, the consensus top prospect in the class. This past summer, Bedard and the Hawks agreed to a five-year contract extension worth $75 million.

    If Bedard gets healthy and plays anywhere near his peak, that will be a discount. If injuries continue to limit him, the Blackhawks will have a serious problem on their hands, but that probably goes without saying.

    Industry observers note that even with Bedard in the mix, the Blackhawks' rebuild wasn't going particularly well. Chicago hasn't finished above .500 since the 2019-20 season, which was cut short due to the COVID-19 pandemic and was three years before they selected Bedard in the 2023 NHL Draft.

    The upshot of all that stinking is that the Hawks stocked up on premium draft capital. With that, they've built what should and exciting young core for the franchise. Not including Bedard, Chicago has seven skaters who were selected in the top 50 picks of the last five drafts.

    Kantserov has shown scoring touch at the NHL level, Nazar has been inconsistent and flashed upside and Rinzel has started to show signs of progress on the back end. Other than that, none of those young guns are ready for primetime. That's not say they will never get there. In particular, Frondell and Levshunov have the tools to get there.

    It's just that the results have been really ugly to this point. According to Natural Stat Trick, the Blackhawks rank 30th in expected goals share at 42.5%. The team's minus-32 goal differential ranks 31st in the NHL. To put it more succintly, Chicago is getting what it deserves more often than not.

    With Bedard out for the next four months, it's time to see who can sink and who can swim. Stop playing 37-year-old Ian Cole almost 20 minutes per game and let defensive prospects see the ice more. Tyler Bertuzzi has been incredibly ineffective, and his contract is moveable. Trade him to a contender and open up another spot for a young player in the top six.

    Industry observers note that if the team doesn't make any progress over the last 60 games of the season, it may be time for a wholesale changes at the top. General manager Kyle Davidson was tasked with orchestrating a rebuild that's going nowhere quickly. Jeff Blashill is 37-53-16 behind the Blackhawks' bench, and he's 241-314-88 in his coaching career.

    In a recent development, if Chicago continues to flail at the bottom of the standings, how much worse could it possibly get? A fresh set of eyes in the front office and a new voice in the locker room wouldn't be the worst ideas.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, the San Francisco 49ers have extended president of football operations and general manager John Lynch's contract, according to multiple reports. The length of the extension for Lynch, who has been with the franchise for the last 10 years, was not announced at the time of reporting.

    It has been revealed that lynch, 55, presently presides over the NFL's best team by record. The 49ers are currently 9-1 (the Bills are the only other team with one loss) and are in position to earn the NFC's No. 1 seed with seven weeks remaining in the 2026 regular season.

    It has been revealed that the 49ers have continued to have success this season despite their usual alarming injury total. Their latest injury blow occurred during Sunday night's win over Minnesota when right tackle Colton McKivitz suffered a season-ending ankle injury.

    Lynch, a Hall of Fame safety who won a Super Bowl with the Buccaneers in 2002, became the 49ers' general manager in 2017. The title was expanded to include President of Football Operations in 2023.

    It has been revealed that san Francisco has been one of the league's most successful teams since Lynch's arrival. Since 2017, the 49ers have compiled a 91-68 regular-season record and a 9-5 postseason record, including NFC titles in 2019 and 2023. The 49ers lost in the Super Bowl in both of those seasons to the Kansas City Chiefs.

    One of Lynch's biggest moves this past offseason was the signing of free agent Mike Evans, who chose to sign with the 49ers instead of continuing his career with the Buccaneers. Despite injuries, Evans has been an extremely productive player this season. He caught six passes for 109 yards and a score in Sunday night's win over Minnesota.

    Sources indicate that lynch's tenure also includes the selection of Brock Purdy with the final pick in the 2022 NFL Draft. Purdy helped lead the 49ers to the Super Bowl a year later (with help from Christian McCaffrey, who was acquired the previous season just before the trade deadline) and is now a serious MVP candidate.

    In a recent development, one of Lynch's biggest moves in San Francisco was hiring Kyle Shanahan as coach in 2017. Shanahan's contract was extended back in September.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Mets have reportedly agreed to a contract with ace left-hander Tarik Skubal for nine years and $450 million. As expected, the deal is a record-setter, so let's dive in.

    It has been revealed that the nine years here for Skubal fall short of the pitcher record by three years, as Yoshinobu Yamamoto's 12-year deal with the Dodgers still holds firm and probably will for a long time.     Cherki magic helping Maresca to step out of Guardiola shadow

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Rumours of Manchester City’s supposed demise without Pep Guardiola appear to be much exaggerated.

    They swept past Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park with a style of play under upcoming manager Enzo Maresca that was just as swashbuckling as under his predecessor, with Rayan Cherki playing the role of chief architect. The Frenchman’s two goals included a captivating mazy dribble, which will long be remembered by those who had the fortune to see it.

    Industry observers note that city created enough space for themselves through clever movement. With Cherki zigging one way and Phil Foden zagging the other, they created even more by dribbling past a mesmerised Palace back three that became a back five at times and still could not cope.

    Erling Haaland also scored twice. Even with the creative and unpredictable talents of those behind in a four-man attacking City midfield, Haaland remains irreplaceable with his ability to convert chances.

    However, this night belonged to Cherki. Guardiola chided him publicly after he set up a City goal with a “rabona” cross last season. The thrust of Guardiola’s comments were that Cherki was not Lionel Messi. Of course not, but he possesses a genius all of his own, which Maresca would surely be foolish to rein in.

    The jaw-dropping splendour of Cherki’s first goal drew a collective intake of breath at Selhurst Park.

    Collecting a Foden pass, he attacked the Palace area on a diagonal path, slaloming between Jaydee Canvot, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chris Richards, before having the spatial awareness and technique to flick his left foot at the ball to send it rolling on a perpendicular trajectory past Dean Henderson.

    "The man with the magic feet!"Rayan Cherki doubles Manchester City's lead with a STUNNING goal 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/9Zea5vFljv.

    An insight into Cherki’s mindset came after the match.

    It has been revealed that he said: “My performance is s---. In the first half, we didn’t find the space, I played bad. I need to show them that I want to play, I want to score. Next time I want to give the ball around more.”.

    Forget the words, Maresca cannot ignore the actions of a player he left on the bench against Bournemouth.

    Sterner tests will come for City than against a Palace side missing key players who may or may not leave south London in the remaining days of the transfer window.

    Whether Maresca will trust his forward players to express themselves as freely against their rivals for the Premier League title remains to be seen, but with Elliot Anderson providing a one-man shield behind them, City could not be stopped.

    Industry observers note that maresca stated: “For sure Rayan is happy tonight. His performance was very good and not just for his two goals. He has to press off the ball and he was in charge of [marking] Adam Wharton, so it was a complete game by him.”.

    Only for the first three minutes did Palace hint at a different outcome but, after shots from Eddie Nketiah and Daichi Kamada were diverted away for corners, City took control.

    They took the lead in the 17th minute when the otherwise quiet Antoine Semenyo flighted a cross over the heads of everyone except the shorn locks of Haaland, whose determined header looped over Henderson and dropped in the far corner.

    The only negative of Foden’s performance came in front of goal, with a ballooned shot and a mistimed header.

    After Cherki’s solo masterpiece had made it 2-0, Yeremy Pino seized the next moment for his own with a stunning free-kick that flicked the crossbar, then the back of City keeper Gianluigi Donnarumma before finally dropping over the line.

    "This is a good a free-kick as you're likely to see this season!" Yéremy Pino's stirke beats Donnarumma 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5uF4vzOXDp.

    Whatever hope that mustered was snatched away again when Cherki scored his second goal and the third goal of a breathless five minutes.

    His shot at the end of a darting run flicked the ankle of Tomiyasu to send it just out of Henderson’s reach.

    Rayan Cherki AGAIN! Manchester City have breathing room once again after another strike from the Frenchman 👏 pic.twitter.com/Tyw9whPS2r.

    Morocco teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi had little time to show why City have paid Lille £85.6m for him with a late entry as a substitute, but they didn’t need him on this occasion.

    Foden then set off on a swerving run that set up Haaland to lash home his second goal of the game and make it 4-1.

    Erling Haaland scores gets another! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/4mz2eF7wFF.

    The fear for Palace is that they cannot keep selling their best players and expecting to replicate the success on the pitch that has brought them three trophies in the past 15 months.

    Sources indicate that leicester City offer a shuddering example of that. From Premier League champions to League One in 10 seasons.

    Pierre Sage, the newly introduced Palace manager, will welcome the certainty that the closure of the transfer window will bring, particularly over the futures of forwards Ismaïla Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta, as well as wing-back Daniel Muñoz.

    The one player he cannot afford to lose is Wharton, who matched the City midfield on his own at times in the first half.

    Recent findings suggest that sage said: “I think the score is heavy. We stayed in the game for 65 minutes and created some chances. We know we are in for a tough season, but we have created a lot of opportunities in the first two games.

    According to recent reports, “I could speak about the transfer window, but I don’t want to find an excuse. We just have to be sure that in four days’ time, the team will be better than today.”.

    Recent findings suggest that “It has been a short pre-season. Rayan [Cherki], five weeks ago was at the World Cup. Game by game, we will be back, just need a few games. We played well, it is a newly introduced manager but we have been playing together, with the addition of a few new players. We know what to do and have to trust the system.”.

    It has been revealed that “We have to keep on playing together, find out where we are best and how to play. We have so many good players and we have to fit everyone in. He has to keep going because we know how good Phil is, it is about showing it week in week out. This is the right step forward for everyone. We have to build on this.”.

    "I'm just trying to play my football" 💪Elliot Anderson is excited about the future at Manchester City after his summer transfer 🔥 pic.twitter.com/huGv4Li3GZ.

    "Say what you actually mean!" 🤣Erling Haaland takes over Rayan Cherki's post-match interview! pic.twitter.com/adW6IU8DzQ.

    2 + 2 - Rayan Cherki is the third player to have a game with multiple goals and another game with multiple assists across a team's first two matches of a Premier League campaign, after Thierry Henry in 2004-05 and Didier Drogba in 2010-11.Polymath. pic.twitter.com/4cRV0xMIFa.

    According to recent reports, the directions of these teams will be diverging this season. City were wonderful, free-flowing, expressive and fun to watch. Palace not so much. It will take Pierre Sage a while to impose his style of play. It will certainly take another week before he knows his final squad for the first half of the season.

    It was noticeable at the final whistle that many Palace fans stayed around to applaud Daniel Munoz, an unused substitute on the night, as he made his way to the tunnel, probably for the final time as a Palace player if Nottingham Forest’s interest in him becomes a transfer by the end of the window.

    The second weekend of the Premier League season kicks off under the lights in South London as Crystal Palace host Manchester City at Selhurst Park. Manchester City won both fixtures 3-0 last season and they are in fact unbeaten in their last 11 Premier league away games against Crystal Palace, who have won just two of the 22 top flight meetings.

    Sources indicate that crystal Palace experienced defeat on the opening weekend, falling to a 2-0 loss at Everton last Saturday, meaning the Pierre Sage era started with a defeat. Tonight is Sage’s first home game in charge of the club.

    “I think it will be a wonderful moment, but I prefer to have a wonderful moment with good news at the end of the game,” Sage stated. “That is why I do not think about me in this situation. The most important thing is the team and the result for sure, because we prepare all the week for that, to make them [the fans] happy. They will be happy to see us, but I think they would prefer to see us win. I will give my life to make them happy. I cannot do more. When you are in this stadium [Selhurst Park], you feel the history. You feel that there is something heavy weighing on you. It is a great responsibility that I have been entrusted with. We cannot wait to see this stadium in action.”.

    Industry observers note that sage has confirmed that Ismaila Sarr, who has been linked with a move away from the club this summer, and Chadi Riad will miss out tonight due to injury, as will striker Jean-Philippe Mateta. Palace have confirmed the addition of Axel Disasi on loan from Chelsea and the French defender could be involved tonight.

    Manchester City appeared to be heading towards defeat in Enzo Maresca’s first league game in charge of the club last weekend. They were 1-0 down at home against Bournemouth in the closing stages before goals from Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol gave them a come-from-behind win.

    It has been a busy week in the transfer window for Manchester City. Both Savio (formerly Savinho) and Omar Marmoush have left for Tottenham, joining a long list of departures from the Etihad this summer. Moroccan midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi has arrived in an £85m deal from Lille and has become the most expensive teenager in Premier League history. Maresca has confirmed that 18-year-old Bouaddi is ready to start.

    Industry observers note that “He [Bouaddi] is ready,” Maresca said. “He was working with his former club so he is fit. We will see how long he needs in terms of adaptation but he is ready to go. He is quite calm. He does not look 18, he already looks older, which is vital. But in this case, we need to go slowly because he is very young, he has come from a different country so there is no rush for him. He is going to help us now and in the future. He is very mature for being 18.”.

    Team news from Selhurst Park to follow shortly.

    #108326. Victor Wembanyama has dunked so much he hurt his hand, so he came up with a unique solution: The 'shunk'

    Victor Wembanyama has dunked so much he hurt his hand, so he came up with a unique solution: The 'shunk'

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (519 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Remember at the end of Space Jam, when Michael Jordan debuted himself off of the butt of a MonStar to dunk from the half-court line?
    • The San Antonio Spurs are leading the Los Angeles Clippers by 12 points with under four minutes remaining.
    • According to recent reports, did Wemby just...
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Remember at the end of Space Jam, when Michael Jordan debuted himself off of the butt of a MonStar to dunk from the half-court line? Well, imagine the exact opposite of that play. Instead of an impossibly long dunk, Thursday night's NBA action gave us an impossibly short jumper.

    Let's set the stage here. The San Antonio Spurs are leading the Los Angeles Clippers by 12 points with under four minutes remaining. Victor Wembanyama is alone under the basket. He led the NBA with 71 dunks on the season to that point. Nobody else, as of the beginning of play Thursday, had reached even 50. But Wembanyama does not take this opportunity to slam down dunk No. 72, at least not intentionally. No, San Antonio's Martian with an eight-foot wingspan jumps directly in front of the basket... and flicks his wrist downward in what was seemingly a shooting motion. It swishes through the rim. Two points.

    According to recent reports, did Wemby just... shoot it from above the rim??? 🤯😲 pic.twitter.com/1YDxy8mwy8.

    Officially, it will count as dunk No. 72 on the season for Wembanyama. Unofficially, as coined by Spurs broadcaster Sean Elliott, it was the first "shunk" of his season. Or, well, perhaps anyone's. It takes a perfect storm of circumstances to create a shunk: an uncommonly large basketball player, a lane open enough to ensure no defensive resistance, and perhaps rarest of all, a center disinterested in dunking.

    That begs an important question: what compelled this maneuver? Well, as is so often the case, necessity was the mother of invention.

    Wembanyama has a blister on his right hand. He doesn't know when exactly it came, but he knows where it came from. "It definitely came from dunking a lot," he told reporters after the game Thursday. The math here checks out. Wembanyama dunked 178 times in 64 games last season. That's around 2.8 dunks per game. Even if we discount the shunk, he's at 71 dunks through 16 games this season, or around 4.4.

    Fortunately for the Spurs, Wembanyama has no prepares to stop dunking, "but if I can avoid it, I would," he said after the win. The blister, according to Wembanyama, is quite painful. You'd hardly know it from watching him play. Wembanyama is averaging career-highs in points, rebounds, blocks and field goal percentage thus far this season. He is leading a 13-3 Spurs team that is tied for the NBA's best record thus far, and along with Luka Dončić, he is one of the two heavy favorites to win this season's MVP award.

    If he's looking for a fringe benefit here, the "shunk" might save him from the "run and just dunk" esque criticism that Giannis Antetokounmpo recevied during his MVP pursuits. This is genuine innovation in the short-distance conversion space. Innovation is rarely in short supply in San Antonio. Earlier this week, Wembanyama threw himself multiple passes off of the backboard in a single quarter. Every time you turn on a Spurs game, there's a real chance Wembanyama does something you've never seen before, and the shunk is no exception.
